requiredDocuments: Loan application form

Address proof

facts.label: Loan type
facts.value: Vehicle finance
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Wheels — vehicle-loan FAQs and shared terms
facts.pageOrSection: Vehicle-loan catalogue and named product classes
facts.quoteOrContext: AU's official Wheels catalogue names car, two-wheeler, three-wheeler, commercial-vehicle, tractor and construction-equipment loans.

facts.label: Maximum finance
facts.value: Up to 100% of the ex-showroom price net of discounts; insurance and registration are excluded. Final amount depends on product and customer profile.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: minimum and maximum Wheels loan amount; ex-showroom price basis
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ states a ₹20,000 minimum and maximum up to 100% of ex-showroom price net of discounts, excluding insurance and registration, based on product and customer profile; the eligible amount uses discounted ex-showroom price.

facts.label: Minimum loan amount
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: minimum and maximum Wheels loan amount
facts.quoteOrContext: The bank states: “The minimum loan amount is ₹20,000” in its Wheels FAQ.

facts.label: Repayment period
facts.value: 6 months to 5 years (60 months); tractor repayment may be quarterly or half-yearly under the common FAQ.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: loan tenure; tractor repayment frequency
facts.quoteOrContext: The Wheels FAQ gives a minimum period of 6 months and maximum of 5 years; a shared tractor FAQ says tractor instalments may be quarterly or half-yearly and schedules can be tailored at bank discretion.

facts.label: Applicant types
facts.value: Individuals and non-individuals: private/public limited companies, partnerships, proprietorships, co-operative societies, trusts and Hindu Undivided Families; subject to the selected Wheels route.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Wheels — vehicle-loan FAQs and shared terms
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: customer categories catered to in Wheels loans
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ lists Individual and Non-individual applicants, then identifies the non-individual entity forms.

facts.label: Documents required
facts.value: Loan application form, identity proof, address proof and other relevant documents. The four-page application form provides a wider case-specific checklist; AU may request additional documents.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank New Car Loan and Vehicle Loan Application Form
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: Documents Required; application form page 4 checklist
facts.quoteOrContext: AU lists application form, identity proof, address proof and other relevant documents. The linked form checklist is broader and explicitly allows additional documents; its items depend on borrower, business, security and loan purpose.

facts.label: Security
facts.value: Normally the financed vehicle or a lien-marked free vehicle/equipment; AU may require additional collateral based on the loan amount or vehicle/equipment.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ says a vehicle financed by AU or lien-marking on free vehicles/equipment is normally acceptable; additional collateral may depend on the requested amount or vehicle.

facts.label: Repayment methods
facts.value: Standing instruction to an AU Small Finance Bank account, cash deposit, cheque or Automated Clearing House (ACH).
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: modes available for repayment of instalments
facts.quoteOrContext: The bank lists standing instructions, cash, cheque and ACH for repayment of instalments.

facts.label: Interest calculation
facts.value: Monthly reducing-balance basis.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.quoteOrContext: AU states interest is calculated on a monthly reducing balance basis.

facts.label: Eligible makes and models
facts.value: AU selects eligible vehicle models based on technology, after-sales support and secondary-market value; confirm the supported model with AU before applying.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Vehicle Loan — shared Wheels FAQs
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: whether finance is available on all vehicle makes
facts.quoteOrContext: The bank says it selects vehicle models based on technology, after-sales support and secondary-market value and asks applicants to confirm models with the branch/support.

facts.label: Accessories
facts.value: Standard manufacturer fitment for vehicle variants may be funded; additional accessories are not funded.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Wheels — vehicle-loan FAQs and shared terms
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ: whether vehicle accessories are funded
facts.quoteOrContext: The common Wheels FAQ says standard manufacturer fitment is funded and additional accessories are not.

facts.label: Interest on overdue instalments
facts.value: At the contracted loan interest rate (Loan IRR).
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Schedule of Charges for Wheels Product (Vehicle Loans), FY 2026–27
facts.pageOrSection: Schedule rows 4–5: interest on overdue instalment
facts.quoteOrContext: The same tariff row applies contracted interest (Loan IRR) to all five vehicle classes.

facts.label: Penal charge for instalment default
facts.value: ₹0.65 per ₹1,000, or part thereof, charged daily on the overdue instalment.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Schedule of Charges for Wheels Product (Vehicle Loans), FY 2026–27
facts.pageOrSection: Schedule row 5: penal charges on instalment default
facts.quoteOrContext: The tariff states ₹0.65 per ₹1,000 (or every part thereof), charged daily on the overdue instalment, for all five vehicle classes.

facts.label: Loan cancellation
facts.value: ₹1,000 if cancelled within 7 days of cheque issue; after that, ₹1,000 plus interest up to the cancellation period. The shared FAQ separately says no cancellation fee before disbursement and case-by-case charges after disbursement; confirm the applicable event/contract before cancellation.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Schedule of Charges for Wheels Product (Vehicle Loans), FY 2026–27
facts.pageOrSection: Schedule row 35; cross-check vehicle-loan FAQ on cancellation before/after disbursement
facts.quoteOrContext: Current schedule row 35 lists ₹1,000 within 7 days of cheque issue, then ₹1,000 plus interest through cancellation; FAQ states no fee before disbursement and case-by-case after disbursement, so trigger details differ and are preserved.

facts.label: Interest rate
facts.value: New: up to 17% p.a.; used: up to 26% p.a.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Rates at a Glance, effective 23 April 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Page 4 of 7: Car loan, new and used rows
facts.quoteOrContext: The current rate sheet gives car loans up to 17% for new and up to 26% for used vehicles; the matching FY 2026–27 Wheels schedule repeats these ceilings.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: For used cars: assessed on income and standard of living, residence stability, equity in the vehicle, established salary or self-employed business cash flow, satisfactory prior credit if any and AU credit norms. The route lists salaried/self-employed, agri/non-agri, rural/semi-urban/urban and new-to-credit/established-credit applicants.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank Used Car Loan — product page
facts.quoteOrContext: Eligibility and applicant segments are listed in the used-car page's dedicated sections.

facts.label: Processing fee
facts.value: New: up to 2% of loan amount; used: up to 3% of loan amount.
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Schedule of Charges for Wheels Product (Vehicle Loans), FY 2026–27
facts.pageOrSection: Tariff rows 1–2, Car column; applicable for FY 2026–27
facts.quoteOrContext: The current schedule caps car processing at 2% for new and 3% for used loans.

facts.label: Documentation charge
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Schedule of Charges for Wheels Product (Vehicle Loans), FY 2026–27
facts.pageOrSection: Tariff row 3: Car, Commercial Vehicle & Construction Equipment, and Tractor/Farm Equipment columns
facts.quoteOrContext: The tariff lists up to INR 5,000 for car, commercial vehicle/construction equipment, and tractor/farm equipment classes.

facts.label: Prepayment / foreclosure charges
facts.value: Base tariff: 5% of balance before 12 months; 4% after 12 months. The same FY 2026–27 schedule states no prepayment charge for floating-rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes and for floating-rate business-purpose loans to individuals/MSEs (loans sanctioned after 1 January 2026). Confirm borrower/entity, purpose, rate type and sanction date against the current contract.

exceptions: floating-rate other-than-business loan to individual borrower
floating-rate business-purpose loan to individual or MSE; sanction after 2026-01-01

facts.unit: percent of outstanding balance, subject to stated exemptions
facts.documentTitle: AU Small Finance Bank — Schedule of Charges for Wheels Product (Vehicle Loans), FY 2026–27
facts.pageOrSection: Tariff row 6 and footnotes under pre-payment/foreclosure; footnote 7
facts.quoteOrContext: The tariff lists 5% before 12 months and 4% after 12 months, then separately exempts qualifying floating-rate business-purpose individual/MSE loans sanctioned after 1 January 2026 and other-than-business floating-rate individual loans. The two written exceptions are retained distinctly.

additionalProperty.name: Loan type
additionalProperty.value: NRI/PIO commercial-real-estate home finance. Bank of Baroda says a third dwelling unit onward, or purchase of a plot, is treated as CRE exposure when an individual already owns two or more houses singly or jointly.

additionalProperty.name: Rate
additionalProperty.value: The current NRI CRE page and the current Retail Loans schedule disagree. The NRI page shows BRLLR −0.50% to +1.70% for CRE and CRE Advantage up to ₹75 lakh, and BRLLR −0.25% to +1.95% for Advantage above ₹75 lakh; the rate page's CRE Max Savings rows show BRLLR −0.45% to +1.30% up to ₹75 lakh and −0.20% to +1.55% above. The NRI page's MITC separately says floating pricing is 1-year MCLR to 1-year MCLR +1%. Confirm the applicable NRI rate with the Bank; no single range is selected.

additionalProperty.name: Benchmark
additionalProperty.value: Conflicting benchmark wording: the NRI page's rate table uses BRLLR spreads and says CRE is 0.25% above the normal NRI/PIO home-loan rate, while its MITC says floating pricing is linked to 1-year MCLR with an annual reset. The current schedule lists 1-year MCLR at 8.75% (effective 12 September 2026) and BRLLR at 7.90% (effective 6 December 2025); its CRE Max Savings floating rows use BRLLR, while a separate MCLR-linked CRE section is labelled effective from 1 April 2016 and sets 0.25%/0.50% over the normal Home Loan rate by amount. The Bank does not reconcile which benchmark or schedule applies to this NRI variant; no borrower rate is calculated.

additionalProperty.name: Minimum income
additionalProperty.value: Combined gross annual income of at least ₹5 lakh equivalent for applicant/co-applicants whose income is counted. The page says applicant/co-applicant income can be combined where an NRI is included.

additionalProperty.name: Eligibility
additionalProperty.value: For NRIs holding Indian passports, PIOs holding foreign passports and OCIs. Applicants may borrow singly or jointly; HUFs are excluded. Counted-income applicants must meet the page's two-year overseas employment/work-permit or overseas residence/business condition and the published combined gross-income floor. The page sets minimum ages of 21 for a borrower and 18 for a co-applicant, and says age may be considered up to 70. Close relatives may co-apply; a non-relative may be considered only if a joint property owner.

additionalProperty.name: Maximum amount
additionalProperty.value: Location-based ceilings: Mumbai ₹10 crore; other metros ₹5 crore; urban areas ₹3 crore. The page repeats the ₹3 crore Urban Areas line twice. Each ceiling remains subject to income, repayment capacity and LTV/margin rules; the CRE page does not list semi-urban or rural ceilings.

additionalProperty.name: Tenure
additionalProperty.value: Maximum loan period is 30 years including a moratorium of up to 36 months. For under-construction houses/buildings through the 7th floor, the page states an 18-month moratorium, then six additional months per floor, capped at 36 months.

additionalProperty.name: Processing fee
additionalProperty.value: Conflicting official terms: the CRE NRI page states a 100% processing-charge waiver for specified DSA/channel/project leads, with ₹3,500–₹10,000 + GST out-of-pocket costs per property; for non-DSA takeover it states nil subject to a refundable ₹1,500 login fee. The current 1 April 2025 tariff separately labels Home Loan (All variants) and prints 50% up to ₹50 lakh or 25% above, with ₹8,500–₹15,000 / ₹8,500–₹25,000 limits and ₹8,500 takeover. The Bank does not reconcile the variant-specific waiver with the all-variants tariff.

additionalProperty.name: Prepayment / foreclosure
additionalProperty.value: The NRI CRE MITC says pre-closure is nil. A separate generic fixed-rate Home Loan tariff says own-source repayment is nil and takeover by another lender costs 0.50% of outstanding. Because the NRI CRE page says fixed pricing was withdrawn but the current bank-wide schedule prints fixed CRE rows without defining NRI applicability, the fixed-rate tariff is not assigned to this borrower variant.

benefits: The shared Max Savings page says each end-of-day credit in the linked savings account is credited against the linked home-loan balance and reduces interest by the same amount; the savings account itself earns zero interest, and the EMI is remitted into it.
The linked account remains available for withdrawal on demand and can use cheque-book, ATM/debit-card, internet-banking and mobile-banking facilities under normal savings-account terms and charges.
Page benefit-image captions also identify a free credit card and free accidental insurance; the reviewed page does not give their cover limits, exclusions or card terms.
Optional group credit-life insurance is described separately; premium and cover conditions are set out in the product facts and table.
eligibilityNotes: Individuals may apply singly or jointly; HUFs are not eligible.

For an applicant/co-applicant whose income is counted, the page requires eligible overseas employment with a valid job contract/work permit for at least the past 2 years, or employment/self-employment/business while staying abroad for at least 2 years.
Minimum gross annual income is equivalent to ₹5 lakh. Where an NRI's income is counted, the page permits the combined applicant/co-applicant income to meet the ₹5 lakh test.

The Bank restricts who may be counted as a co-applicant; non-relatives may be considered only as joint property owners. See the published eligibility table for the listed close-relative relationships and PIO/OCI definitions.
requiredDocuments: The current NRI forms listing links a general 18-page Home Loan application packet with 2022 file metadata; its pages 12–13 request NRI employment, identity, bank/income, guarantor, PIO and property documents listed below. It is not labelled Max Savings-specific.

Salaried NRI applicants: employment contract (translated into English and attested by employer or Indian Embassy if not in English), latest 6 months' certified salary slips, employer ID, Continuous Discharge Certificate where applicable, current work permit, visa-stamped passport and latest NRE account passbook/statement.

Other income/banking evidence requested in the form: latest 6 months' overseas bank statements; biodata with qualifications, current job details and proof; 2 years' Indian/foreign income-tax returns; salary certificate/income statement attested by the foreign office/competent authority or notarised if attestation is unavailable; employer undertaking to remit instalments where required by sanction.

Self-employed/business NRI applicants: 3 years' business/profession balance sheets and profit-and-loss statements plus individual income-tax returns, CA-certified; business profile describing nature, organisation, customers and suppliers.
PIO evidence: PIO card or current passport showing place of birth; previous Indian passport; and parents'/grandparents' passports, as applicable to the claimed PIO route.

Property papers vary by case. The form lists purchase-payment receipts, approved drawings, construction permission, applicable Urban Land Ceiling permission, sale agreement/deed or cost estimate, co-operative allotment letter, and scenario-specific builder, society, resale, authority or plot-construction papers.
A guarantor form and guarantor net-worth/income evidence are requested where a guarantor is applicable.

The currently listed 6-page generic Model Checklist for Retail Loans adds baseline application, identity/residence, financial, property, NRI/PIO and self-employed items; it expressly says product-specific requirements may be added. It is older generic guidance, not a Max Savings-specific mandate. Its full checklist is retained separately so conditional and other-product items are not mistaken for universal requirements.
The product page's exact checklist link was inaccessible in this review; this application-form list must not be read as a complete current Max Savings checklist.

additionalProperty.value: Resident Indians, NRIs/PIOs/OCIs and eligible staff may transfer an eligible home loan from a bank, HFC, NBFC or financial institution. facts.label: Loan type
facts.value: Home loan linked to a Bank of Baroda savings account, where each end-of-day credit balance reduces the amount on which home-loan interest is calculated.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Max Savings Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: The sanctioned loan is linked with a savings account; end-of-day account credit is counted against the linked home-loan account for interest reduction.

facts.label: Interest offset
facts.value: The daily end-of-day balance in the linked savings account reduces the home-loan balance used for interest calculation; the linked savings account itself earns 0% interest.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Max Savings Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: Any credit in the linked savings account at the end of the day reduces the interest-bearing home-loan balance to the extent of that credit; the linked savings account rate is zero.

facts.label: EMI recovery
facts.value: The borrower deposits the monthly instalment into the linked savings account; the product page lists automatic EMI recovery.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Max Savings Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower remits EMIs into the linked savings account and the feature list states automatic recovery EMI.

facts.label: Rate conditions
facts.value: Pricing depends on loan limit and CIBIL score. A 0.05% risk premium applies when the borrower does not obtain credit-insurance cover. The Bank says its concessions apply to floating-rate facilities only.
facts.documentTitle: Retail Loans Interest Rates — applicable Home Loan notes
facts.quoteOrContext: Rate depends on loan limit and CIBIL score; 0.05% risk premium without credit insurance; Bank concessions apply to floating-rate facilities only.

facts.quoteOrContext: Maximums are stated for Mumbai, other metros, Hyderabad/New Delhi/Bengaluru, urban, semi-urban/rural and Chandigarh tri-city, subject to income, repayment capacity and LTV/margin.

facts.value: For NRI/PIO/OCI applicants whose income is counted, combined gross annual income must be at least ₹5 lakh. The page does not state one resident-applicant minimum salary; residents are assessed using the published repayment-capacity bands.

facts.label: Repayment tenure
facts.value: Up to 30 years including a maximum 36-month moratorium. For under-construction homes through the 7th floor, the stated moratorium is 18 months, then 6 additional months per floor, capped at 36 months.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Max Savings Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: Maximum initial period 30 years includes a moratorium up to 36 months; 18 months up to seventh floor with 6 more months per additional floor to 36 months.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Resident Indians and eligible NRIs, PIOs and OCIs; individual applicants may apply singly or jointly, but HUFs are not eligible. Resident counted-income applicants need 1 year of salaried employment or 2 years in business/profession (up to 3 months' service break). Counted-income NRI/PIO/OCI applicants need 2 years' qualifying overseas work/business residence and combined gross annual income of ₹5 lakh. Borrower age starts at 21; co-applicant at 18; age may be considered up to 70. Close relatives may co-apply; a non-relative must be a joint property owner.

facts.label: NRI, PIO and OCI eligibility definitions
facts.value: The Bank's PIO definition covers citizens other than Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, China, Iran, Nepal and Bhutan who previously held an Indian passport; whose parent or grandparent was an Indian citizen under the stated law; or who are the spouse of an Indian citizen or qualifying person. Its OCI section requires OCI registration and PIO status under the page's description, lists ancestry/territory eligibility paths and minor children, and excludes a person who has ever been a citizen of Pakistan or Bangladesh. These are the Bank page's stated definitions, not independent legal advice.

facts.label: Co-applicant rules
facts.value: Close relatives may join as co-applicants for higher eligibility. A non-close-relative may be considered only if they jointly own the property; in that case, another close relative who is not a joint owner should not be added to raise eligibility. The Bank's listed close relatives are spouse; father; mother (including stepmother); son (including stepson); son's wife; daughter (including stepdaughter); daughter's husband; brother/sister (including stepsiblings); brother's wife; spouse's sister (including stepsister); sister's husband; and spouse's brother (including stepbrother).

benefits: Daily end-of-day balance in the linked savings account reduces the home-loan balance used for interest calculation; the linked savings account pays 0% interest.
The borrower deposits EMIs into the linked account; the page describes automatic EMI recovery and use of otherwise idle funds.
Floating-rate bands are linked to BRLLR. At the published 7.90% BRLLR, the listed floating spreads calculate to 7.20%–9.20% p.a. depending on loan size and borrower pricing.
Optional group credit-life insurance is available to home-loan borrowers; it is borrower-paid and may be financed subject to eligibility and LTV rules.
eligibilityNotes: The scheme is for resident Indians and eligible NRIs holding Indian passports, PIOs holding foreign passports, and OCIs; the MITC also identifies Bank staff availing under a public scheme.

Applicants may apply singly or jointly; HUFs are excluded. Resident income-counted applicants need at least 1 year in salaried employment or 2 years in business/profession; up to a 3-month service break may be allowed.
For an NRI/PIO/OCI whose income is counted, the page requires at least 2 years of eligible overseas employment/business residence and combined counted gross annual income of at least ₹5 lakh.

Borrower minimum age is 21 years; co-applicant minimum age is 18 years. The MITC says maximum age may be considered up to 70 years; the standard Home Loan page has a conflicting age-at-maturity/retirement FAQ, which is not silently imported as a Max Savings-specific rule.

Close relatives may join as co-applicants. A non-relative may be considered only if they are a joint owner of the financed property; the page imposes an additional restriction where another close relative is not a joint owner.
Resident applicants have published repayment-capacity limits by net monthly income; this is not a fixed rupee minimum-income threshold.
requiredDocuments: The current Max Savings page links to a Home Loan checklist PDF, but that exact official link timed out on 23 September 2026; its detailed checklist contents remain unresolved.
The current download-forms listing includes the Home Loan application and generic retail-loan documents. These listing entries do not establish a complete Max Savings-specific document checklist.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Student must be going abroad for professional or technical studies and be admitted to the notified institution and course; admission may be through the listed entrance-test or merit-selection route. The FAQ says there is no specific age restriction for the student, and the loan can cover MBA, MCA and MS abroad.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The page requires admission to a notified institution/course and the FAQ confirms no specific student-age restriction and MBA/MCA/MS eligibility.

facts.label: Fixed-rate prepayment

facts.pageOrSection: Interest rates & charges — Pre-payment charges under fixed rate loan

facts.label: Maximum repayment tenure
facts.value: Repayable in maximum 10–15 years after the moratorium. The moratorium is the course period plus one year for the standard Baroda Scholar guideline; repayment is capped at 120 instalments for loans up to ₹7.50 lakh and 180 instalments above ₹7.50 lakh.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — official product page
facts.quoteOrContext: The official repayment section states maximum 10–15 years after the moratorium, with 120 instalments up to ₹7.50 lakh and 180 instalments above it.

facts.label: Repayment tenure

facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC gives 10–15 years after moratorium and 120/180 instalment caps by loan amount.

facts.label: Margin
facts.value: Premier institutions: nil up to ₹4 lakh, 15% above ₹4 lakh through ₹7.50 lakh, and nil above ₹7.50 lakh. Non-premier institutions: nil up to ₹4 lakh, 15% above ₹4 lakh through ₹7.50 lakh, and 10% above ₹7.50 lakh.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC publishes separate premier and non-premier margin bands by ₹4 lakh and ₹7.50 lakh thresholds.

facts.label: Moratorium
facts.value: Course period plus one year.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC states the repayment holiday/moratorium is the course period plus one year.

facts.label: Covered expenses
facts.value: College/institution/university/hostel/mess fees; examination, library and laboratory fees; books, equipment, instruments and uniforms; required computers/laptops; caution, building or refundable deposits supported by institutional bills/receipts up to 10% of total course tuition; student-borrower insurance premium; study tours, project work and thesis; and travel/passage money. External coaching or tuition is excluded.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC enumerates fees, materials, deposits capped at 10% of tuition, insurance, study/travel expenses and excludes external coaching/tuition.

facts.label: Security
facts.value: Up to ₹4 lakh: parent co-obligation and no security. Above ₹4 lakh to ₹7.50 lakh: suitable third-party guarantee plus assignment of future income. Above ₹7.50 lakh to ₹80 lakh: tangible collateral equal to 100% of the loan plus future-income assignment. Above ₹80 lakh: total security coverage of 1.25 times the loan plus future-income assignment. The page repeats the 100% tangible-collateral rule for loans above ₹7.50 lakh; the selected sanction band should be confirmed.
facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC lists parent co-obligation/no security up to ₹4 lakh, third-party guarantee through ₹7.50 lakh, 100% tangible collateral through ₹80 lakh and 1.25x above ₹80 lakh; a later paragraph repeats the above-₹7.50-lakh rule.

facts.label: Disbursement
facts.value: Direct to school/institution/hostel term-wise or year-wise in stages according to requirement or demand; direct to book sellers/shops for books, instruments and equipment. facts.documentTitle: Baroda Scholar — current official page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC provides staged direct disbursement and a verified direct-payment route for self-arranged lodging where no institute hostel exists.

benefits: Location-based maximums: ₹20 crore in Mumbai; ₹7.50 crore in Hyderabad, New Delhi and Bengaluru; ₹5 crore in other metros and Chandigarh, Panchkula and Mohali; ₹3 crore in urban areas; ₹1 crore in semi-urban and rural areas.
BRLLR-linked interest resets monthly; interest is calculated on a daily-reducing balance.
Repayment can run up to 30 years, including a moratorium of up to 36 months under the published construction-stage/possession rules.
Nil processing charge; the current schedule separately lists ₹8,500 out-of-pocket expenses per property. GST is excluded from the stated schedule.
No prepayment penalty; the Yoddha MITC lists pre-closure charges as nil.
Optional IndiaFirst group credit-life cover is borrower-paid; its one-time premium depends on borrower and loan details and may be financed subject to LTV.
The page says other variants, including Home Improvement, Home Loan Advantage Top Up and Home Suvidha, may be available under Bank guidelines.
eligibilityNotes: Target groups: Indian Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard personnel; Central Forces personnel of Assam Rifles, Border Security Forces, Indo-Tibetan Border Police, Sashastra Seema Bal, Central Industrial Security Force and Central Reserve Police Force.
Serving employees are eligible. Retired pensioners must also be gainfully employed or engaged in business/profession for at least 1 year if salaried or 2 years if non-salaried.
For applicants/co-applicants whose income is counted, the page requires at least 1 year of salaried employment or 2 years in business/profession; a service break up to 3 months may be allowed.
Minimum age: borrower 21 years and co-applicant 18 years. The Bank says maximum age may be considered up to 70 years.
Close relatives under the Baroda Home Loan definition may join as co-applicants. A non-relative may be considered only if they jointly own the property.
Published income-band rules are FOIR repayment-capacity limits, not a minimum salary threshold; the current page gives no fixed rupee minimum income.
requiredDocuments: Yoddha-specific: employment certificate signed by the Commanding Officer or Officer Commanding, showing applicant name, rank, unit, service number, ID-card number, photograph, signature and the certificate's purpose.
The Yoddha page also requires the documents in the linked Baroda Home Loan checklist. That exact checklist PDF timed out; do not treat the following general BOB guide as a replacement checklist.

General BOB home-loan guide: completed and signed application; 2 passport-size photographs; one identity proof (PAN, Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or voter ID); age proof (PAN, Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or birth certificate); and permanent-address proof (Aadhaar, passport, driving licence, bank passbook or utility bill).

Salaried applicants: Form 16, employer letter confirming employment and duration, salary slips for the last 3–6 months, filed income-tax returns for the last 3 years, salary-credit account statement and investment proof if any.

Self-employed applicants: business-address proof, filed tax returns for the last 3 years, CA-audited/attested balance sheet and profit-and-loss statements, applicable business/professional licence and establishment registration, and business-account statement.

Property papers as applicable: society/builder NOC; registered sale deed, allotment letter or stamped sale agreement; occupancy certificate for ready properties; maintenance/utility bills and property-tax receipts; advance-payment receipts; building plan; land-tax/possession records; seller/builder payment statement; and construction-cost estimate for construction loans.
The bank's guide says requirements can vary by application, employment and property type; the linked checklist and branch assessment may request additional papers.

facts.label: CSIS eligibility
facts.value: For PM-USP CSIS, the student must take an IBA Model Education Loan for an eligible technical or professional course in India and have gross parental/family income from all sources up to ₹4.50 lakh a year. products.summary: BoB Housing Loans for EWS, LIG & MIG with government subsidy benefits. Get affordable urban housing finance, quick approvals, low interest rates, flexible repayment, and PMAY CLSS eligibility. Apply now!
products.geographicAvailability: India; eligibility, branch and channel availability follow the official product terms

facts.label: Age and housing eligibility
facts.value: Minimum age 21 and maximum age 60; applicant may own no home or one home, must self-declare it, and the house carpet area is up to 60 sq m in an urban or metro centre.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Urban Areas
facts.quoteOrContext: The official features section publishes age, home-ownership and carpet-area criteria.

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: Purchase or construction of a new home, purchase of a built home, additions, repairs, or renovation; standalone plot purchase is not allowed, although land plus construction may be financed within the project-cost limit.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Urban Areas
facts.quoteOrContext: The official purpose section lists permitted uses and excludes standalone plot purchase.

facts.label: Maximum home finance
facts.value: Metro centres: ₹35 lakh with maximum project cost ₹45 lakh. Other centres: ₹25 lakh with maximum project cost ₹30 lakh. Home improvement: ₹10 lakh metro and ₹6 lakh other centres.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Urban Areas
facts.quoteOrContext: The official maximum-loan table publishes separate metro, other-centre and improvement limits.

facts.label: Fees
facts.value: Processing charge is stated as nil; legal and valuation out-of-pocket expenses are recovered at actual cost capped at ₹5,000 plus GST.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Urban Areas
facts.quoteOrContext: The official fee section publishes nil processing charge and the ₹5,000 plus GST legal/valuation cap.

facts.label: Security / route
facts.value: Applications originate through the Jan Samarth portal and are governed by applicable RBI, LTV, credit-appraisal and Bank of Baroda home-loan rules. Security is the equitable mortgage of the financed property.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Urban Areas
facts.quoteOrContext: The official terms and FAQ publish the Jan Samarth route and equitable-mortgage security.

facts.label: Loan type
facts.value: Home loan
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals - Urban Areas — official product page
facts.pageOrSection: Official product name and loan classification
facts.quoteOrContext: The official product name identifies this as “Home Loan scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals - Urban Areas”.

facts.label: Maximum annual income
facts.value: Applicant annual income up to ₹9 lakh; a regular income source and at least 12 months of Bank-account or UPI transaction history are required.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Urban Areas
facts.quoteOrContext: The official page publishes the ₹9 lakh income ceiling and 12-month account/UPI history requirement.

facts.label: Benchmark
facts.value: Bank of Baroda says BRLLR applies to all retail lending products. The current page lists BRLLR at 7.90% (repo 5.25% + markup/base spread 2.65%) effective 6 December 2025 and 1-year MCLR at 8.75% effective 12 August 2026. Product-specific spreads, CIBIL pricing and scheme conditions determine the applicable rate.
facts.documentTitle: Bank of Baroda Retail Loans Interest Rates
facts.pageOrSection: MCLR benchmark; BRLLR benchmark; retail loan rate tables
facts.quoteOrContext: The page states that BRLLR was introduced for all retail lending products and gives the current BRLLR, repo-plus-spread composition and MCLR reference. It does not state that one single spread applies to every product.

facts.label: Rate
facts.value: Not published as a product-specific rate on the EWS/LIG/MIG page. The page says the scheme is governed by Bank of Baroda home-loan rules and RBI/LTV/credit-appraisal norms, but does not map a spread or effective rate to this scheme.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG and MIG Individuals — official product page
facts.quoteOrContext: The Interest rates & charges section only states nil fees and the terms section refers to home-loan rules; no EWS/LIG/MIG rate is published on the page.

facts.label: APR
facts.value: Not published as a separate APR for this scheme. The page does not provide an all-in annual percentage rate.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG and MIG Individuals — official product page
facts.quoteOrContext: The complete current page and FAQ were reviewed; no APR calculation appears.

facts.label: Tenure
facts.value: The page's home-loan FAQ states a maximum home-loan term of 30 years, ending no later than retirement or age 65, whichever is earlier; it does not publish a separate EWS/LIG/MIG-specific term.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan Scheme for EWS, LIG and MIG Individuals — official product page
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ — average tenure of a home loan
facts.quoteOrContext: The product page's FAQ gives the bank's standard home-loan term rule; the scheme sections do not provide a different term.

facts.label: Prepayment
facts.value: Part or full prepayment from the borrower’s own sources is permitted. The reviewed EWS/LIG/MIG page does not state a percentage or rupee prepayment charge for this scheme; applicable Bank of Baroda home-loan rules and the sanction terms govern any charge.
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals — Bank of Baroda official product page
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ — ‘But can I prepay the loan ahead of schedule?’; Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ says the borrower may prepay the loan in part or in full from own sources. No charge amount is printed for this scheme on the page.

facts.label: Maximum amount
facts.value: Home-loan limits are ₹35 lakh in metro centres (project cost up to ₹45 lakh) and ₹25 lakh elsewhere (project cost up to ₹30 lakh).
facts.documentTitle: Home Loan scheme for EWS, LIG & MIG Individuals - Urban Areas — official product page
facts.pageOrSection: Published loan terms in product summary
facts.quoteOrContext: The manually reviewed product summary states: “Home-loan limits are ₹35 lakh in metro centres (project cost up to ₹45 lakh) and ₹25 lakh elsewhere (project cost up to ₹30 lakh).”.

benefits: Urban/metro home finance for EWS/LIG/MIG applicants with regular income and digital banking/economic footprints, including unorganised-sector workers and PMAY-U 2.0 beneficiary groups.
Home-loan limits are ₹35 lakh in metro centres (project cost up to ₹45 lakh) and ₹25 lakh elsewhere (project cost up to ₹30 lakh).
Home-improvement limits are ₹10 lakh in metro centres and ₹6 lakh elsewhere; salary slips, Form 16 and several ITR/balance-sheet documents are not required.
eligibilityNotes: Applicant annual income must be up to ₹9 lakh; minimum age is 21 and maximum age is 60.
A satisfactorily maintained Bank account or UPI transaction history for at least 12 months is required, and primary banking must move to Bank of Baroda before disbursement.
Applicant may own no home or one home and must provide a self-declaration; residential carpet area is capped at 60 sq m.
Purpose includes purchase/construction, purchase of a built home, additions, repairs and renovation; standalone plot purchase is not allowed.
requiredDocuments: Home-loan checklist documents, KYC, property papers and evidence of the 12-month account/UPI history.
Self-declaration of owning no home or one home and income/digital-footprint evidence as assessed by the Bank.
Salary slips, Form 16, ITR acknowledgements, advance-tax challans and certified balance sheets/P&L are expressly not required under this scheme.

benefits: Use income from an idle property.
Deposit surplus money to save interest.
Flexibility to withdraw money.
Available as a demand loan.
Competitive interest rate.
Loan available up to ₹25 crore.
eligibilityNotes: Applicant must be an NRI holding a valid Indian passport.

Minimum gross annual income, averaged over the last 3 years, is ₹5 lakh, including co-applicant income counted for the limit.

requiredDocuments: Duly filled and signed application form with photograph.
Passport copy with visa stamp.
Proof of residence in India and abroad (driving licence, ration card, voter ID, passport, Aadhaar or registered rent agreement).
Name, relationship, address and contact details of a local contact person.
NRE savings-account statement for the last 6 months.
Overseas bank-account statement for the last 6 months, including salary account where applicable.
Statements of all existing loan accounts for the last year; for BOB loans, account number and customer ID in the application.
Overseas credit-bureau report, if already obtained.
PIO evidence where applicable: current passport showing Indian birth place, earlier Indian passport, or parent/grandparent passport substantiating PIO status.
Salaried applicants: employment contract, certified salary slips for the last 6 months, current-employer identity card, continuous discharge certificate where applicable and latest work permit.

Self-employed applicants: balance sheets and profit-and-loss accounts, individual income-tax returns for the last 3 years, business/profession note, business proof (any two valid registrations), place-of-business address proof and continuous discharge certificate where applicable.

Property documents as applicable: agreement for sale, approved blueprint, non-agriculture certificate, commencement/completion/occupancy certificates, latest property-tax receipt, society/share certificate, builder/seller payment receipts, development agreement, chain of earlier agreements, advocate title-clearance report and bank-approved valuation report.
For takeover: existing loan account statement, property-document list acknowledged by the existing lender, sanction letter and foreclosure letter where available.

facts.label: Penal charges for late payment and sanction breaches
facts.value: BOB's schedule effective 1 April 2026 sets overdue charges by loan classification: for priority-sector loans, nil below ₹50,000 sanctioned; 1% p.a. of default above ₹50,000 through ₹2,00,000; 2% p.a. above ₹2,00,000. The document does not assign exactly ₹50,000 in the priority-sector bands, and the PM Vidyalaxmi pages do not identify this account's priority-sector classification. The PDF also lists other sanction breaches at 2% p.a. of outstanding, but its closing note says penal charges apply solely to overdue payments; those statements conflict. Its cap is 4% p.a. overall, calculated monthly for the actual default period, with no further penal charge on an earlier penal amount.

benefits: Interest rates start from 6.85% p.a. for eligible institutions.
100% finance with no maximum cap published.

Admission/offer letter from the QHEI with the course fee structure or expense schedule.

facts.unit: percentage of eligible project cost/TFO; conditions apply

facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 6.3.1–6.3.8 state the 36%/44% back-ended composite subsidy, total-loan cap, subsidy-reserve interest treatment, three-year lock-in, current-repayment condition and final-instalment adjustment.

facts.label: Subsidy project-cost ceiling
facts.value: For subsidy calculations: ₹20 lakh TFO for an individual project; up to ₹25 lakh for an approved extremely successful individual project; up to ₹100 lakh for a group of at least five trained persons. A bank may finance a group of 2–4 trained persons under a ₹20 lakh-per-trained-person subsidy TFO ceiling. Actual bank credit may exceed the subsidy ceiling if the bank finds the project technically feasible and financially viable.
facts.unit: TFO ceiling for subsidy, not an absolute loan cap
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2 labels these as project-cost ceilings for subsidy and separately states that actual bank credit may be higher based on viability and technical feasibility.

facts.label: Programme loan structure
facts.value: Credit linked to AC&ABC subsidy is a composite term loan covering fixed capital and one operating cycle of working capital. Sanctioned loan is the total financial outlay less margin; at least 10% of project outlay must be in capital form. Repayment is 5–10 years with a maximum two-year grace period; the rate follows RBI guidelines and the financing bank's declared policy.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 5.3.1–5.3.5 specify the composite term-loan components, margin deduction, 10% minimum capital share, 5–10-year repayment, up to two-year grace, and bank/RBI interest-policy basis.

facts.label: Programme service charge
facts.value: Banks may levy a service charge up to 2% per annum under the programme; this is a service-charge ceiling, not the product's processing fee.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.4.2 says participating banks may levy service charges up to 2% per annum; this is kept separate from bank processing-fee schedules.

facts.label: Project completion deadline
facts.value: Complete the project within 6 months of the first loan disbursement. The financing institution may extend this by a further 6 months for justifiable reasons; if the project is not complete within 1 year, subsidy is unavailable and any advance subsidy must be refunded.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.6 sets six months from first disbursement, a further six-month extension for justified reasons, and subsidy loss/refund after one year.

facts.label: AC&ABC training
facts.value: The programme includes a 45-day training course. Candidates bear their own travel costs to and from the training institute; the course covers venture selection, market survey and preparation of a detailed project report with banker support.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium specifies a 45-day training programme, states that the candidate bears travel to and from the institute, and describes venture selection, market survey and DPR preparation with banker support.

facts.label: Co-borrower option for trained women
facts.value: Parents, husbands or in-laws of a trained woman candidate may be co-borrowers, and the project may retain subsidy eligibility.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2.4 allows parents, husbands or in-laws of trained women to be co-borrowers while remaining eligible for subsidy.

facts.label: Programme margin and shortfall support
facts.value: Margin follows RBI guidance and prevailing bank norms. For SC/ST, women, North-Eastern State and Hill-area beneficiaries, NABARD may support the financing bank for up to 50% of the prescribed margin shortfall, without interest, if the bank is satisfied that the borrower cannot meet the margin.
facts.unit: margin / percentage of prescribed margin shortfall
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The document says margin is governed by RBI and bank norms; for specified beneficiary groups NABARD may provide the bank up to 50% of prescribed margin to meet a shortfall when the bank is satisfied the borrower cannot meet it.

facts.label: Extension-service condition for subsidy
facts.value: Delivery of extension services to farmers is a component of an AC&ABC project for subsidy eligibility. The centre's service model may charge farmers or provide services free, according to local needs and affordability.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The objectives and definitions allow paid or free extension services based on the agri-preneur's model and local affordability; §6.1.2 makes extension-service delivery a component of subsidised AC&ABC projects.

facts.label: Insurance of project assets
facts.value: The participating bank should ensure that assets created under the project are insured where insurance is required by law. If the beneficiary chooses insurance when it is not legally required, that cost is an eligible component of total financial outlay.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.7.2 requires insurance where statutorily required and allows voluntarily chosen asset insurance expense in the TFO.

facts.label: Application and bank decision
facts.value: Submit the bank-prescribed term-loan/subsidy application with a MANAGE-vetted project report through the nodal training institute using the Jan Samarth or Agriculture Infrastructure Fund portal. The bank is to decide acceptance or rejection within 30 days and notify the applicant; this is a stated process timeline, not a promise of approval.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The DPR is submitted with the application through Jan Samarth or AIF; §6.4.1 sets a 30-day bank decision timeline and notification to the applicant.

facts.label: Repeat subsidy and same-project restriction
facts.value: A candidate may take a more beneficial Central or State subsidy for the field, but the same project cannot receive subsidy from more than one scheme. AC&ABC subsidy may be used up to twice for a candidate across eligible independent projects or expansion/phased financing; the combined TFO ceiling still applies, and expansion subsidy is calculated only on incremental project outlay.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 6.3.4–6.3.5 prohibit dual-scheme subsidy for the same project, allow AC&ABC subsidy up to twice, and limit expansion claims to incremental TFO subject to the combined ceiling.

facts.label: Assessment for the ₹25 lakh exceptional-project ceiling
facts.value: The programme's subsidy TFO may rise from ₹20 lakh to ₹25 lakh for an extremely successful individual project. The scoring grid requires at least 75 of 100 marks and Empowered Steering Committee approval on the banker's recommendation. The grid classifies 50% as a successful establishment and 75% as an extremely successful project.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.pageOrSection: PDF p.13 §5.2.2; PDF p.38 Annexure X
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2.2 requires a minimum 75 marks and approval by the Empowered Steering Committee based on the banker's recommendation; Annexure X defines the 100-mark grid and 50%/75% categories.

facts.label: Programme subsidy-claim timeline
facts.value: After first loan disbursement, the bank is to send the subsidy claim within 45 days. On receipt of a complete bank application, NABARD's regional office is to forward it to Head Office within 30 days; Head Office's stated release window is 7 days after the regional recommendation, subject to available Government subsidy funds. These are programme administration timelines, not a guaranteed borrower payout date.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium sets 45 days for the bank claim after first disbursement, 30 days for the regional office to forward a complete file, and a 7-day Head Office release window after recommendation subject to fund availability.

facts.label: Bank and programme age-rule discrepancy
facts.value: Bank of Maharashtra's current product page states 18–60; the Government AC&ABC Programme-2025 states 21–60. For applicants aged 18–20, these official criteria disagree; confirm the applicable rule with the bank before applying.
facts.documentTitle: Financing for Setting Up of Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centers for Agriculture Graduates — Bank of Maharashtra
facts.pageOrSection: Eligibility, rendered lines 500–508 and FAQ 2, lines 540–542; compared with Government Programme-2025 §3, PDF p.3
facts.quoteOrContext: The live Bank of Maharashtra product table and FAQ say ages 18 to 60; the Government Programme-2025 says 21 to 60. This remains an unresolved bank/programme discrepancy.

facts.label: KCC rules for new sanctions from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027, RBI requires a six-year composite facility for crop and allied working capital plus agriculture/allied investment credit. Loans sanctioned earlier remain under the existing directions until maturity or next renewal. The new directions do not set one universal interest rate: bank pricing and Government interest support continue under the applicable rules.

long-term agriculture and allied investment credit

facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 2, 4, 8–10 and 21; issued 19 June 2026, applicable from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraph 2 sets the commencement and transition; paragraphs 8–10 define the six-year composite facility and limit components; paragraph 21 leaves rate setting to the applicable advances directions and agriculture-loan guidance.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

normalizedValue.cropWorkingCapital: current season notified Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area
normalizedValue.termLoanLimit: proposed investment and bank assessment of repayment capacity

facts.unit: limit-calculation method; not a guaranteed sanction amount
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 13(1)–13(7), 19 and 20; crop drawing limit and investment-credit limit
facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.

facts.label: KCC rules for new sanctions from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027, RBI requires a six-year composite facility for crop and allied working capital plus agriculture/allied investment credit. Loans sanctioned earlier remain under the existing directions until maturity or next renewal. The new directions do not set one universal interest rate: bank pricing and Government interest support continue under the applicable rules.

normalizedValue.appliesTo: KCC loans sanctioned on or after effective date by commercial banks covered by the RBI Directions, including SBI
normalizedValue.priorLoanTransition: Earlier sanctions remain under extant directions until maturity or next renewal
components: short-term crop and allied working capital
long-term agriculture and allied investment credit

facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 2, 4, 8–10 and 21; issued 19 June 2026, applicable from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraph 2 sets the commencement and transition; paragraphs 8–10 define the six-year composite facility and limit components; paragraph 21 leaves rate setting to the applicable advances directions and agriculture-loan guidance.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

normalizedValue.cropWorkingCapital: current season notified Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area
normalizedValue.termLoanLimit: proposed investment and bank assessment of repayment capacity

facts.unit: limit-calculation method; not a guaranteed sanction amount
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 13(1)–13(7), 19 and 20; crop drawing limit and investment-credit limit
facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.

requiredDocuments: For a new or deepened well: Ground Water Directorate feasibility certificate, except for the page's stated well-desalting-after-torrential-rain-collapse and existing-well stone-revetment/parapet exceptions.

facts.label: KCC rules for new sanctions from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027, RBI requires a six-year composite facility for crop and allied working capital plus agriculture/allied investment credit. Loans sanctioned earlier remain under the existing directions until maturity or next renewal. The new directions do not set one universal interest rate: bank pricing and Government interest support continue under the applicable rules.

facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 2, 4, 8–10 and 21; issued 19 June 2026, applicable from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraph 2 sets the commencement and transition; paragraphs 8–10 define the six-year composite facility and limit components; paragraph 21 leaves rate setting to the applicable advances directions and agriculture-loan guidance.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.

products.summary: Group-based credit for individual members to start, improve or expand income-generating activities, including agricultural allied activities. benefits: Finance may support starting, improving or expanding income-generating activities, including allied agricultural activity.

eligibilityNotes: Each member's individual income must not exceed ₹50,000 per year.
Members must have been permanent residents of the area for the previous 3 years and live within 16 km of the branch; members should preferably live in a cluster.
No more than one person from a family may be included in a group.

Members must not belong to another SHG or MCG. The MCG or its members must not be borrowers or defaulters to another bank, financial institution or co-operative society; the page requires a declaration.
For debt-swap finance, the member must have borrowed from a moneylender at least 1 year before applying and undertake not to borrow from a moneylender again.
Members execute an agreement making all group members jointly and severally liable for loans availed by members.

facts.pageOrSection: Section J — Scheme for financing small tractors (up to30HP)

facts.documentTitle: Farm Machinery Loans — Canara Bank; Rate of Interest for Agriculture & Allied Activities
facts.label: Eligibility (Farm Machinery tractor route)
facts.value: If booked through Canara’s Farm Machinery Loans route: for tractors up to 35 HP, at least 6 acres perennially irrigated or 12 acres dry land, plus 1,000–1,200 work hours yearly including at least 500 hours on the farmer’s own land. The tractor must be on Canara’s approved list and suit the soil, cropping pattern and landholding. The bank separately names a small-tractor rate scheme up to 30 HP but does not explicitly cross-reference the eligibility page to that rate row.
facts.pageOrSection: Farm Machinery Loans page lines 331–337; agriculture rate PDF p.3, Section J
facts.quoteOrContext: Canara’s page covers tractor finance and gives one eligibility band for tractors up to 35 HP. Section J of the rate PDF separately names the Small Tractor Scheme up to 30 HP. The fact is shown with a Farm Machinery route condition because the bank does not explicitly state that the standalone rate row uses that product page’s eligibility terms.

facts.documentTitle: Farm Machinery Loans — Canara Bank; Rate of Interest for Agriculture & Allied Activities
facts.label: Margin (Farm Machinery route)
facts.value: If booked through Canara’s Farm Machinery Loans route: nil up to ₹2 lakh; 15%–25% of invoice above ₹2 lakh; 40% for second-hand tractors. The bank has not expressly assigned these margin bands to the separate Small Tractor Scheme rate row.
facts.pageOrSection: Farm Machinery Loans page lines 343–345; agriculture rate PDF p.3, Section J
facts.quoteOrContext: The margin bands are from Canara’s Farm Machinery Loans page, whose financed machinery includes tractors. The exact Small Tractor Scheme is separately named in the rate schedule; route applicability remains explicit and conditional.

facts.documentTitle: Farm Machinery Loans — Canara Bank; Rate of Interest for Agriculture & Allied Activities
facts.label: Security (Farm Machinery route)
facts.value: For a new tractor booked through Canara’s Farm Machinery Loans route: up to ₹2 lakh, hypothecation of the machinery; above ₹2 lakh, hypothecation plus a mortgage of land worth at least the loan amount, or eligible tangible security with the required margin and value equivalent to the loan amount. The bank has not expressly assigned this security rule to the separate Small Tractor Scheme rate row.
facts.pageOrSection: Farm Machinery Loans page lines 346–348; agriculture rate PDF p.3, Section J
facts.quoteOrContext: The security rules are explicitly for new tractors and other listed farm machinery. They are retained as a conditional Farm Machinery route term, not represented as an unqualified scheme-specific rule.

facts.documentTitle: Farm Machinery Loans — Canara Bank; Rate of Interest for Agriculture & Allied Activities
facts.label: Repayment period (Farm Machinery route)
facts.value: If booked through Canara’s Farm Machinery Loans route: repay within 5–9 years in half-yearly or yearly instalments, depending on income generation. The bank does not separately state this tenure against the Small Tractor Scheme rate row.
facts.pageOrSection: Farm Machinery Loans page line 349; agriculture rate PDF p.3, Section J
facts.quoteOrContext: The page states the repayment period for Farm Machinery Loans. The rate PDF separately lists the small-tractor pricing route but gives no tenure; the route qualification is preserved.

facts.documentTitle: Canara penal charges for credit facilities — updated 12 December 2025; Small Tractor Scheme rate schedule
facts.label: Prepayment / transfer charge (conditional)
facts.value: Canara’s policy waives prepayment penal charges for floating-rate business-purpose loans to individuals and MSEs, without a minimum lock-in. For a floating-rate term loan to a non-individual borrower other than an MSE, a 2% charge on the amount prepaid applies when the borrower requests transfer to another bank or financial institution. Dual/special-rate loans follow the rate type at prepayment. The Small Tractor rate is one-year MCLR-linked; confirm borrower type and the sanctioned rate in the loan documents.
facts.pageOrSection: Policy physical pp.8–9, item 19 (effective 01-01-2026); rate schedule p.3, Section J
facts.quoteOrContext: The current policy ties charges to transfer to another bank/FI, borrower type and fixed/floating status. Its term-loan footnote bases any charge on the amount prepaid. The product’s published rate is MCLR-linked; no unconditional prepayment fee is inferred for every borrower.

products.name: Canara PMEGP
customerSegments: Individuals aged above 18 setting up a new viable non-farm micro-enterprise under PMEGP in a rural or urban area.
products.summary: Credit-linked finance for new micro-enterprises under PMEGP. Project cost eligible for margin-money subsidy is capped at ₹50,00,000 for manufacturing and ₹20,00,000 for service/business; the bank may consider additional finance without subsidy.
products.geographicAvailability: India, for eligible rural and urban projects. Some business/trading and transport activities have location-specific restrictions under PMEGP.
benefits: Subsidy-eligible project cost up to ₹50,00,000 for manufacturing and ₹20,00,000 for service/business.
Government margin-money subsidy ranges from 15% to 35% by beneficiary category and rural/urban location.
Beneficiary contribution is 10% for general category and 5% for special category; banks finance 90% or 95% respectively.
Canara publishes repayment from 3 to 7 years and an initial moratorium up to 6 months; the Ministry guideline phrases the period as after the bank-prescribed moratorium.
RBI advises collateral-free PMEGP loans up to ₹20,00,000 for loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 April 2026.
No income ceiling applies under the current PMEGP portal eligibility rules.
eligibilityNotes: Applicant must be an individual above 18 years and the project must be a new unit; existing units or units that have already received government subsidy under another scheme are not eligible for the new-unit route.
At least VIII-standard pass is required when project cost is above ₹10,00,000 in manufacturing or above ₹5,00,000 in business/service.
Only one person per family may receive new-unit assistance; the current portal defines family as self, spouse and unmarried children.
Projects need capital expenditure, must meet local rules and the PMEGP negative list, and must register on Udyam before physical verification and subsidy adjustment.
The current official Canara page also contains an expired Madhya Pradesh scheme block ending 31 March 2025 and mis-grouped handloom limits; neither is a PMEGP new-unit eligibility condition.
requiredDocuments: Customer identification proof and Canara NF-998 MSME application
Address proof for the unit and promoters
Applicable licences and permissions
Financial papers for the last 3 years with income-tax returns and projections, as listed on Canara's page
Guarantor details with proof of assets, as listed on Canara's page
Stock statement, as listed on Canara's page
See the product-page table for the older NF-998 form's conditional, indicative checklist; it is not a universal PMEGP checklist.

facts.label: Own contribution and subsidy
facts.value: General category: 10% own contribution and margin subsidy of 15% in urban or 25% in rural areas. Special category: 5% own contribution and subsidy of 25% urban or 35% rural. The bank finances the remaining 90% or 95% respectively; subsidy is held and adjusted under scheme rules.

facts.pageOrSection: Canara page lines 341-345; Ministry guideline PDF pp.3-4
facts.quoteOrContext: The category/location percentages match the live Canara and Ministry scheme tables. Special categories are the list printed by the source and include SC, ST, OBC, minorities, women, ex-servicemen, transgender, differently-abled, NER, aspirational districts and notified hill/border areas.

facts.label: Working-capital share of project cost
facts.value: Working capital may be up to 40% of project cost for manufacturing and up to 60% for service/trading projects.
facts.documentTitle: Revised PMEGP Scheme Guidelines, including Udyam modification
facts.quoteOrContext: The scheme guideline caps the working-capital portion at 40% for manufacturing and 60% for service/trading.

facts.label: Project-cost treatment
facts.value: Project cost combines capital expenditure and working capital. Land cost is excluded. A ready-built or rented/leased workshop may be counted for at most 3 years. Canara's page additionally states that building investment should not exceed 100% of plant/equipment cost; the current portal and reviewed guideline do not restate that ratio, so confirm it against the current sanction checklist.
facts.documentTitle: PMEGP project-cost terms — Ministry of MSME and Canara Bank
facts.quoteOrContext: The portal excludes land and limits ready-built/rented/leased workspace to 3 years. Canara's separate 100% building-to-machinery statement is retained as a bank-page claim but not represented as a current Ministry-wide rule.

facts.label: When the subsidy is adjusted
facts.value: Margin-money subsidy is kept in a beneficiary-named TDR/SRF for 3 years. No interest is paid on that deposit, and no loan interest is charged on the corresponding loan portion. Adjustment follows the lock-in and required physical verification; assistance is one-time except for the separate second-loan upgradation route.
facts.documentTitle: Revised PMEGP Scheme Guidelines, including Udyam modification
facts.quoteOrContext: Guidelines require three-year TDR/SRF holding, no interest on the TDR/SRF, and no loan interest on the corresponding amount; adjustment follows verification and an agency letter.

facts.label: Entrepreneurship training
facts.value: For subsidy claim, EDP training is required. The guideline sets at least 5 days for projects up to ₹5,00,000 and at least 10 days above ₹5,00,000; training is not mandatory for projects up to ₹2,00,000. Prior qualifying training can exempt a repeat course. Canara's page still shows a 12-day optional module, which conflicts with the current portal/guideline treatment.

facts.quoteOrContext: The page publishes institute-category and joint-borrower conditions.

facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 2, 4, 8–10 and 21; issued 19 June 2026, applicable from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraph 2 sets the commencement and transition; paragraphs 8–10 define the six-year composite facility and limit components; paragraph 21 leaves rate setting to the applicable advances directions and agriculture-loan guidance.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

normalizedValue.termLoanLimit: proposed investment and bank assessment of repayment capacity

facts.unit: limit-calculation method; not a guaranteed sanction amount
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 13(1)–13(7), 19 and 20; crop drawing limit and investment-credit limit
facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 23–25 and 32–33; applicable to KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraphs 23–25 define the collateral/margin waivers; paragraphs 32–33 make insurance optional, require explicit consent for KCC-funded premium and assign funded insurance to the lender.

customerSegments: Resident individuals aged 18–70, including salaried, self-employed, farmer, homemaker and student applicants; homemakers and students need an income co-applicant.
products.summary: A secured loan against eligible gold jewellery or specified bank-issued coins, with bullet, monthly-interest and EMI repayment options. Published amount, tenure and rate depend on the selected repayment scheme and sanction.

eligibilityNotes: The product page lists resident individuals aged 18–70; a guarantor is not required. Homemakers and students require an income co-applicant.

Accepted collateral: 18–22 carat jewellery and IDFC FIRST Bank-issued gold coins up to 50 g per customer. Bullion, other coin types, gold bars/idols/utensils/watches, white gold, sub-18-carat ornaments and items that cannot be valued are excluded.

facts.label: How gold is valued
facts.value: The bank uses the lower of the preceding 30-day average closing price for the gold's specific purity or the preceding day's price published by India Bullion and Jewellers Association. Non-gold stones/gems and attached materials are deducted; lower-purity eligible jewellery is converted proportionately to 22-carat fine weight. Stone/acid, saltwater and magnet tests are mandatory; other listed tests may be additional or not apply to every item.
