facts.label: AC&ABC programme eligibility
facts.value: The Government AC&ABC Programme-2025 is open to candidates aged 21–60 with an eligible agriculture/allied qualification. It requires at least a one-year gap after qualification before training. This is the programme's eligibility rule; bank product-page criteria are shown separately.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The programme is open to candidates aged 21 to 60; its text sets a one-year minimum gap after qualification for candidates to be considered for training.

facts.label: Indian Bank-listed qualification routes
facts.value: Agriculture/allied graduates; a three-year post-+2 agriculture/allied diploma with at least 50% marks; or a postgraduate diploma in agriculture/allied subjects. The page also requires at least a one-year gap after qualification before training.
facts.documentTitle: Agri Clinic and Agri Business Centres (ACABC) — Indian Bank
facts.pageOrSection: Eligibility and Training and Handholding, rendered lines 339–349
facts.quoteOrContext: The page lists age and qualification requirements, a one-year gap before training, 45-day training and subsidy-linked credit.

facts.label: Credit age after training
facts.value: After training, the programme permits a credit facility up to age 62.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium sets the upper age for obtaining credit after training at 62.

facts.label: Subsidy eligibility
facts.value: Serving persons and retired persons receiving pensionary benefits are not eligible for AC&ABC subsidy.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 3 expressly excludes serving persons and retired servants receiving pensionary benefits from subsidy benefits.

facts.label: Composite subsidy
facts.value: Back-ended composite subsidy on eligible project cost/TFO: 36% for other eligible candidates; 44% for women, SC/ST, persons with disabilities and all candidates from North-Eastern and Hill States. The subsidy is capped at the total loan amount, covers fixed capital plus one operating cycle of working capital, bears no interest after credit to the Subsidy Reserve Fund and is excluded from the interest-bearing loan component. Minimum lock-in: 3 years; subsidy requires repayments to be up to date and is adjusted in one lump sum against the last instalments.
facts.unit: percentage of eligible project cost/TFO; conditions apply
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 6.3.1–6.3.8 state the 36%/44% back-ended composite subsidy, total-loan cap, subsidy-reserve interest treatment, three-year lock-in, current-repayment condition and final-instalment adjustment.

facts.label: Subsidy project-cost ceiling
facts.value: For subsidy calculations: ₹20 lakh TFO for an individual project; up to ₹25 lakh for an approved extremely successful individual project; up to ₹100 lakh for a group of at least five trained persons. A bank may finance a group of 2–4 trained persons under a ₹20 lakh-per-trained-person subsidy TFO ceiling. Actual bank credit may exceed the subsidy ceiling if the bank finds the project technically feasible and financially viable.
facts.unit: TFO ceiling for subsidy, not an absolute loan cap
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2 labels these as project-cost ceilings for subsidy and separately states that actual bank credit may be higher based on viability and technical feasibility.

facts.label: Programme loan structure
facts.value: Credit linked to AC&ABC subsidy is a composite term loan covering fixed capital and one operating cycle of working capital. Sanctioned loan is the total financial outlay less margin; at least 10% of project outlay must be in capital form. Repayment is 5–10 years with a maximum two-year grace period; the rate follows RBI guidelines and the financing bank's declared policy.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 5.3.1–5.3.5 specify the composite term-loan components, margin deduction, 10% minimum capital share, 5–10-year repayment, up to two-year grace, and bank/RBI interest-policy basis.

facts.label: Programme service charge
facts.value: Banks may levy a service charge up to 2% per annum under the programme; this is a service-charge ceiling, not the product's processing fee.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.4.2 says participating banks may levy service charges up to 2% per annum; this is kept separate from bank processing-fee schedules.

facts.label: Project completion deadline
facts.value: Complete the project within 6 months of the first loan disbursement. The financing institution may extend this by a further 6 months for justifiable reasons; if the project is not complete within 1 year, subsidy is unavailable and any advance subsidy must be refunded.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.6 sets six months from first disbursement, a further six-month extension for justified reasons, and subsidy loss/refund after one year.

facts.label: AC&ABC training
facts.value: The programme includes a 45-day training course. Candidates bear their own travel costs to and from the training institute; the course covers venture selection, market survey and preparation of a detailed project report with banker support.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium specifies a 45-day training programme, states that the candidate bears travel to and from the institute, and describes venture selection, market survey and DPR preparation with banker support.

facts.label: Co-borrower option for trained women
facts.value: Parents, husbands or in-laws of a trained woman candidate may be co-borrowers, and the project may retain subsidy eligibility.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2.4 allows parents, husbands or in-laws of trained women to be co-borrowers while remaining eligible for subsidy.

facts.label: Programme margin and shortfall support
facts.value: Margin follows RBI guidance and prevailing bank norms. For SC/ST, women, North-Eastern State and Hill-area beneficiaries, NABARD may support the financing bank for up to 50% of the prescribed margin shortfall, without interest, if the bank is satisfied that the borrower cannot meet the margin.
facts.unit: margin / percentage of prescribed margin shortfall
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The document says margin is governed by RBI and bank norms; for specified beneficiary groups NABARD may provide the bank up to 50% of prescribed margin to meet a shortfall when the bank is satisfied the borrower cannot meet it.

facts.label: Extension-service condition for subsidy
facts.value: Delivery of extension services to farmers is a component of an AC&ABC project for subsidy eligibility. The centre's service model may charge farmers or provide services free, according to local needs and affordability.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The objectives and definitions allow paid or free extension services based on the agri-preneur's model and local affordability; §6.1.2 makes extension-service delivery a component of subsidised AC&ABC projects.

facts.label: Insurance of project assets
facts.value: The participating bank should ensure that assets created under the project are insured where insurance is required by law. If the beneficiary chooses insurance when it is not legally required, that cost is an eligible component of total financial outlay.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.7.2 requires insurance where statutorily required and allows voluntarily chosen asset insurance expense in the TFO.

facts.label: Application and bank decision
facts.value: Submit the bank-prescribed term-loan/subsidy application with a MANAGE-vetted project report through the nodal training institute using the Jan Samarth or Agriculture Infrastructure Fund portal. The bank is to decide acceptance or rejection within 30 days and notify the applicant; this is a stated process timeline, not a promise of approval.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The DPR is submitted with the application through Jan Samarth or AIF; §6.4.1 sets a 30-day bank decision timeline and notification to the applicant.

facts.label: Repeat subsidy and same-project restriction
facts.value: A candidate may take a more beneficial Central or State subsidy for the field, but the same project cannot receive subsidy from more than one scheme. AC&ABC subsidy may be used up to twice for a candidate across eligible independent projects or expansion/phased financing; the combined TFO ceiling still applies, and expansion subsidy is calculated only on incremental project outlay.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 6.3.4–6.3.5 prohibit dual-scheme subsidy for the same project, allow AC&ABC subsidy up to twice, and limit expansion claims to incremental TFO subject to the combined ceiling.

facts.label: Assessment for the ₹25 lakh exceptional-project ceiling
facts.value: The programme's subsidy TFO may rise from ₹20 lakh to ₹25 lakh for an extremely successful individual project. The scoring grid requires at least 75 of 100 marks and Empowered Steering Committee approval on the banker's recommendation. The grid classifies 50% as a successful establishment and 75% as an extremely successful project.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.pageOrSection: PDF p.13 §5.2.2; PDF p.38 Annexure X
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2.2 requires a minimum 75 marks and approval by the Empowered Steering Committee based on the banker's recommendation; Annexure X defines the 100-mark grid and 50%/75% categories.

facts.label: Programme subsidy-claim timeline
facts.value: After first loan disbursement, the bank is to send the subsidy claim within 45 days. On receipt of a complete bank application, NABARD's regional office is to forward it to Head Office within 30 days; Head Office's stated release window is 7 days after the regional recommendation, subject to available Government subsidy funds. These are programme administration timelines, not a guaranteed borrower payout date.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium sets 45 days for the bank claim after first disbursement, 30 days for the regional office to forward a complete file, and a 7-day Head Office release window after recommendation subject to fund availability.

facts.label: KCC rules for new sanctions from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027, RBI requires a six-year composite facility for crop and allied working capital plus agriculture/allied investment credit. Loans sanctioned earlier remain under the existing directions until maturity or next renewal. The new directions do not set one universal interest rate: bank pricing and Government interest support continue under the applicable rules.

normalizedValue.appliesTo: KCC loans sanctioned on or after effective date by commercial banks covered by the RBI Directions, including SBI
normalizedValue.priorLoanTransition: Earlier sanctions remain under extant directions until maturity or next renewal
components: short-term crop and allied working capital
long-term agriculture and allied investment credit

facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 2, 4, 8–10 and 21; issued 19 June 2026, applicable from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraph 2 sets the commencement and transition; paragraphs 8–10 define the six-year composite facility and limit components; paragraph 21 leaves rate setting to the applicable advances directions and agriculture-loan guidance.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

normalizedValue.cropWorkingCapital: current season notified Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area
normalizedValue.termLoanLimit: proposed investment and bank assessment of repayment capacity

facts.unit: limit-calculation method; not a guaranteed sanction amount
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 13(1)–13(7), 19 and 20; crop drawing limit and investment-credit limit
facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 23–25 and 32–33; applicable to KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraphs 23–25 define the collateral/margin waivers; paragraphs 32–33 make insurance optional, require explicit consent for KCC-funded premium and assign funded insurance to the lender.

facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 2, 4, 8–10 and 21; issued 19 June 2026, applicable from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraph 2 sets the commencement and transition; paragraphs 8–10 define the six-year composite facility and limit components; paragraph 21 leaves rate setting to the applicable advances directions and agriculture-loan guidance.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

normalizedValue.cropWorkingCapital: current season notified Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area
normalizedValue.termLoanLimit: proposed investment and bank assessment of repayment capacity

facts.unit: limit-calculation method; not a guaranteed sanction amount
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 13(1)–13(7), 19 and 20; crop drawing limit and investment-credit limit
facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.
facts.documentTitle: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card Scheme) Directions, 2026
facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 23–25 and 32–33; applicable to KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027
facts.quoteOrContext: Paragraphs 23–25 define the collateral/margin waivers; paragraphs 32–33 make insurance optional, require explicit consent for KCC-funded premium and assign funded insurance to the lender.

requiredDocuments: PNB's current forms catalogue lists PNB Form 1235 for agricultural-credit applications above ₹2 lakh. Its page-7 checklist asks for self-attested photo identity (Voter ID, Driving Licence, PAN, Aadhaar, passport or another government photo ID); recent residence proof (including a telephone/electricity bill, property-tax receipt not older than two months, or accepted government/local-authority identity or address document); two applicant photographs not older than six months; and land-record particulars. The form also collects applicant/family, land/crop, income, asset/liability, security and guarantor details. Its checklist is indicative and non-exhaustive. PNB does not state that this individual agricultural-credit form/checklist applies unchanged to every ACABC project or applicant type, so scheme/entity-specific requirements remain to be confirmed.

facts.label: Composite subsidy
facts.value: Back-ended composite subsidy on eligible project cost/TFO: 36% for other eligible candidates; 44% for women, SC/ST, persons with disabilities and all candidates from North-Eastern and Hill States. The subsidy is capped at the total loan amount, covers fixed capital plus one operating cycle of working capital, bears no interest after credit to the Subsidy Reserve Fund and is excluded from the interest-bearing loan component. Minimum lock-in: 3 years; subsidy requires repayments to be up to date and is adjusted in one lump sum against the last instalments.

facts.value: For subsidy calculations: ₹20 lakh TFO for an individual project; up to ₹25 lakh for an approved extremely successful individual project; up to ₹100 lakh for a group of at least five trained persons. A bank may finance a group of 2–4 trained persons under a ₹20 lakh-per-trained-person subsidy TFO ceiling. Actual bank credit may exceed the subsidy ceiling if the bank finds the project technically feasible and financially viable.

facts.quoteOrContext: The tariff describes takeover by a non-individual borrower and separately states exemptions. Product applicability depends on the final borrower type, facility and rate type; do not show this as a universal fee.

facts.label: AC&ABC programme eligibility
facts.value: The Government AC&ABC Programme-2025 is open to candidates aged 21–60 with an eligible agriculture/allied qualification. It requires at least a one-year gap after qualification before training. This is the programme's eligibility rule; bank product-page criteria are shown separately.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The programme is open to candidates aged 21 to 60; its text sets a one-year minimum gap after qualification for candidates to be considered for training.

facts.label: PNB-listed qualification routes
facts.value: Agriculture/allied graduates; specified diploma or postgraduate-diploma holders; agriculture/allied postgraduates; recognised degrees with more than 60% agriculture/allied course content; specified biological-sciences graduates with agriculture diplomas; or agriculture-related intermediate courses with at least 55% marks. Some qualifications from other agencies require Government approval on State recommendation.
facts.documentTitle: Agriclinic and Agribusiness Centres Scheme (ACABC) — PNB scheme PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: Retained from PNB's complete single-page scheme sheet so moving the programme age rule into its own fact does not discard PNB's listed qualification routes.

facts.label: Credit age after training
facts.value: After training, the programme permits a credit facility up to age 62.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium sets the upper age for obtaining credit after training at 62.

facts.label: Subsidy eligibility
facts.value: Serving persons and retired persons receiving pensionary benefits are not eligible for AC&ABC subsidy.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 3 expressly excludes serving persons and retired servants receiving pensionary benefits from subsidy benefits.

facts.label: Programme loan structure
facts.value: Credit linked to AC&ABC subsidy is a composite term loan covering fixed capital and one operating cycle of working capital. Sanctioned loan is the total financial outlay less margin; at least 10% of project outlay must be in capital form. Repayment is 5–10 years with a maximum two-year grace period; the rate follows RBI guidelines and the financing bank's declared policy.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 5.3.1–5.3.5 specify the composite term-loan components, margin deduction, 10% minimum capital share, 5–10-year repayment, up to two-year grace, and bank/RBI interest-policy basis.

facts.label: Programme service charge
facts.value: Banks may levy a service charge up to 2% per annum under the programme; this is a service-charge ceiling, not the product's processing fee.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.4.2 says participating banks may levy service charges up to 2% per annum; this is kept separate from bank processing-fee schedules.

facts.label: Project completion deadline
facts.value: Complete the project within 6 months of the first loan disbursement. The financing institution may extend this by a further 6 months for justifiable reasons; if the project is not complete within 1 year, subsidy is unavailable and any advance subsidy must be refunded.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.6 sets six months from first disbursement, a further six-month extension for justified reasons, and subsidy loss/refund after one year.

facts.label: AC&ABC training
facts.value: The programme includes a 45-day training course. Candidates bear their own travel costs to and from the training institute; the course covers venture selection, market survey and preparation of a detailed project report with banker support.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium specifies a 45-day training programme, states that the candidate bears travel to and from the institute, and describes venture selection, market survey and DPR preparation with banker support.

facts.label: Co-borrower option for trained women
facts.value: Parents, husbands or in-laws of a trained woman candidate may be co-borrowers, and the project may retain subsidy eligibility.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2.4 allows parents, husbands or in-laws of trained women to be co-borrowers while remaining eligible for subsidy.

facts.label: Programme margin and shortfall support
facts.value: Margin follows RBI guidance and prevailing bank norms. For SC/ST, women, North-Eastern State and Hill-area beneficiaries, NABARD may support the financing bank for up to 50% of the prescribed margin shortfall, without interest, if the bank is satisfied that the borrower cannot meet the margin.
facts.unit: margin / percentage of prescribed margin shortfall
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The document says margin is governed by RBI and bank norms; for specified beneficiary groups NABARD may provide the bank up to 50% of prescribed margin to meet a shortfall when the bank is satisfied the borrower cannot meet it.

facts.label: Extension-service condition for subsidy
facts.value: Delivery of extension services to farmers is a component of an AC&ABC project for subsidy eligibility. The centre's service model may charge farmers or provide services free, according to local needs and affordability.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The objectives and definitions allow paid or free extension services based on the agri-preneur's model and local affordability; §6.1.2 makes extension-service delivery a component of subsidised AC&ABC projects.

facts.label: Insurance of project assets
facts.value: The participating bank should ensure that assets created under the project are insured where insurance is required by law. If the beneficiary chooses insurance when it is not legally required, that cost is an eligible component of total financial outlay.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.7.2 requires insurance where statutorily required and allows voluntarily chosen asset insurance expense in the TFO.

facts.label: Application and bank decision
facts.value: Submit the bank-prescribed term-loan/subsidy application with a MANAGE-vetted project report through the nodal training institute using the Jan Samarth or Agriculture Infrastructure Fund portal. The bank is to decide acceptance or rejection within 30 days and notify the applicant; this is a stated process timeline, not a promise of approval.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The DPR is submitted with the application through Jan Samarth or AIF; §6.4.1 sets a 30-day bank decision timeline and notification to the applicant.

facts.label: Repeat subsidy and same-project restriction
facts.value: A candidate may take a more beneficial Central or State subsidy for the field, but the same project cannot receive subsidy from more than one scheme. AC&ABC subsidy may be used up to twice for a candidate across eligible independent projects or expansion/phased financing; the combined TFO ceiling still applies, and expansion subsidy is calculated only on incremental project outlay.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: Sections 6.3.4–6.3.5 prohibit dual-scheme subsidy for the same project, allow AC&ABC subsidy up to twice, and limit expansion claims to incremental TFO subject to the combined ceiling.

facts.label: Assessment for the ₹25 lakh exceptional-project ceiling
facts.value: The programme's subsidy TFO may rise from ₹20 lakh to ₹25 lakh for an extremely successful individual project. The scoring grid requires at least 75 of 100 marks and Empowered Steering Committee approval on the banker's recommendation. The grid classifies 50% as a successful establishment and 75% as an extremely successful project.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.pageOrSection: PDF p.13 §5.2.2; PDF p.38 Annexure X
facts.quoteOrContext: Section 5.2.2 requires a minimum 75 marks and approval by the Empowered Steering Committee based on the banker's recommendation; Annexure X defines the 100-mark grid and 50%/75% categories.

facts.label: Programme subsidy-claim timeline
facts.value: After first loan disbursement, the bank is to send the subsidy claim within 45 days. On receipt of a complete bank application, NABARD's regional office is to forward it to Head Office within 30 days; Head Office's stated release window is 7 days after the regional recommendation, subject to available Government subsidy funds. These are programme administration timelines, not a guaranteed borrower payout date.
facts.documentTitle: Compendium of Instructions for Implementation of Revised Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Programme 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The compendium sets 45 days for the bank claim after first disbursement, 30 days for the regional office to forward a complete file, and a 7-day Head Office release window after recommendation subject to fund availability.

facts.label: Borrower margin
facts.value: For ACABC loans up to ₹5 lakh, margin is nil; above ₹5 lakh, margin is 25%. PNB's general note says back-ended subsidy does not remove the borrower's required margin contribution under applicable bank/government rules.
facts.documentTitle: PNB General Guidelines for Agricultural Credit — current ACABC clauses

facts.quoteOrContext: The current page's named ACABC row sets nil margin through ₹5 lakh and 25% above; its general note says back-ended subsidy does not remove the prescribed borrower margin.

facts.label: Security
facts.value: For an ACABC loan up to ₹10 lakh, hypothecation of assets created from the loan is sufficient and no further security is required. PNB refers to tiny-industry norms above ₹10 lakh but publishes no separate numeric collateral threshold in this clause.

facts.label: Agriculture-credit application and document checklist
facts.value: PNB's current forms catalogue lists PNB Form 1235 for agricultural-credit applications above ₹2 lakh. Its page-7 checklist asks for self-attested photo identity (Voter ID, Driving Licence, PAN, Aadhaar, passport or another government photo ID); recent residence proof (including a telephone/electricity bill, property-tax receipt not older than two months, or accepted government/local-authority identity or address document); two applicant photographs not older than six months; and land-record particulars. The form also collects applicant/family, land/crop, income, asset/liability, security and guarantor details. Its checklist is indicative and non-exhaustive. PNB does not state that this individual agricultural-credit form/checklist applies unchanged to every ACABC project or applicant type, so scheme/entity-specific requirements remain to be confirmed.

Standalone secondary processing is excluded; the crop-wise list is illustrative, not exhaustive.

products.name: PNB Guruji Student Credit Card Scheme
customerSegments: Students pursuing eligible higher education under the Government of Jharkhand scheme
products.summary: Jharkhand’s Guruji scheme provides an education term loan through participating banks, including PNB. The scheme lists loans up to ₹15 lakh; after state interest support, the student rate is 3% or 4% simple p.a., depending on interest paid during study.
benefits: Loan up to ₹15 lakh for an eligible course at a qualifying institution
Student rate after state subsidy: 3% simple p.a. when interest is paid during study, or 4% when it is not
No income ceiling is stated in the scheme FAQ
No processing fee and no prepayment charge are stated in the official FAQ
eligibilityNotes: Applicant must be aged 40 or younger and must not already have received the scheme benefit.

Admission to an eligible institution is required. The Jharkhand connection may be shown by a valid local-residence certificate, or by the schooling route: Class 10 in a recognised Jharkhand school for a diploma; Class 10 plus Class 12/diploma from a Jharkhand school, college or university for a degree.

The official sources conflict on the institution ranking cutoff: the Gazette amendment and FAQ state top 200 overall or top 100 in the relevant NIRF domain, while one current portal institution-list section says top 100 overall. Confirm the institution with the scheme/participating bank before applying.
An active loan for the same course must be closed and a no-objection certificate obtained before applying under the amended rule.
A co-applicant is required; the participating bank makes its own credit decision.
requiredDocuments: Class 10 marksheet and certificate
Class 12 marksheet and certificate, where applicable to the course route
Jharkhand local-residence certificate or the applicable Jharkhand schooling records
Student Aadhaar and co-applicant Aadhaar
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar for online application OTP verification
Student photograph and signature; co-applicant photograph and signature
Student bank passbook front page or cancelled cheque; co-applicant passbook or cheque
Admission proof and institution/course fee structure
No-objection certificate if an existing loan for the same course has been closed

facts.quoteOrContext: The portal states a student rate of 4% when study-period interest is not paid and 3% when it is paid; both are simple interest after subsidy.

facts.pageOrSection: Current interest rate section; FAQ Q7 cross-check

facts.value: No income ceiling for applying under the scheme.
facts.documentTitle: Guruji Student Credit Card Scheme complete FAQ
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ explicitly answers that there is no income ceiling for candidates to apply.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: For eligible Jharkhand students admitted to a qualifying higher-education course/institution: age 40 or younger; local-residence certificate, or Class 10 in Jharkhand for diploma, or Class 10 plus Class 12/diploma from a Jharkhand school/college/university for degree; no previous scheme benefit. Close an ongoing same-course loan and obtain an NOC before applying. Parent/legal guardian co-applicant required. facts.pageOrSection: Eligibility modal, institution list and application checklist; Gazette amendment clauses on domicile, course/institution and same-course loans
facts.quoteOrContext: The portal, FAQ and 2024 amendment establish the age, admission, residency/schooling, prior-beneficiary and existing-loan rules; the ranking threshold differs between the Gazette/FAQ and one portal list panel.

facts.label: Eligible institutions
facts.value: The 2024 amendment and FAQ specify NIRF top 200 overall or top 100 in the relevant domain, or NAAC grade A or above, plus institutions of national importance/eminent status; all IHM, NIFT and NID institutions; government medical colleges and deemed universities in Jharkhand for MBBS, PG or specialization; XISS, NIAMT, BIT Sindri, CIPET Ranchi and Birsa Agriculture University. One current portal institution-list panel instead says top 100 overall; confirm the cutoff with the scheme/MLI.
facts.documentTitle: Official Gazette amendment to Guruji scheme guidelines, 2024
facts.pageOrSection: Amendment clause expanding eligible institutions; compare portal Institution List panel and FAQ eligibility answers
facts.quoteOrContext: The amendment provides top-200 overall/top-100 domain or NAAC A criteria and names additional institution groups; the live portal's list panel shows a stricter top-100 overall threshold.

facts.label: Permitted education expenses
facts.value: Covers qualifying institutional course/tuition fees; hostel and mess costs and refundable deposits/examination/library/laboratory charges when included in the institution fee structure; and study materials/equipment supplied by the institution when included in that structure. Up to 30% of total sanction may be used for specified non-institutional course-period costs.
facts.documentTitle: Guruji Student Credit Card Scheme complete FAQ and original Detailed Guidelines
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ course-expense answers; original 2023 Guidelines printed pp. 2–4, provisions not changed by the amendment
facts.quoteOrContext: The official FAQ and detailed guideline tie several institutional expenses to their inclusion in the institution fee structure and set a maximum 30% share for eligible non-institutional expenses.

facts.label: Non-institutional expenses
facts.value: Up to 30% of the total sanctioned loan over the course: eligible items include rent/PG, food outside the institution, approved study trips/conferences/seminars/competitions, travel home, specified medical aids for students with disabilities, and daycare/childcare for women with children aged 0–5. Advance is subject to semester limits and supporting bills; later claims depend on settlement of earlier claims.
facts.documentTitle: Guruji Student Credit Card Scheme FAQ and Detailed Guidelines

facts.quoteOrContext: The official material limits eligible non-institutional use to 30% of total sanction and requires valid bills/documents for reimbursement/claims.

facts.value: Nil for sanctioned loans up to ₹4 lakh; 5% when sanction exceeds ₹4 lakh. Scholarship or other assistance is included in margin and is applied pro rata as amounts are disbursed.

facts.pageOrSection: FAQ margin-money question; original 2023 Guidelines printed pp. 15–16, not amended in Gazette
facts.quoteOrContext: FAQ states no margin up to ₹4 lakh and 5% above ₹4 lakh; scholarship/assistance is counted toward margin.

facts.pageOrSection: FAQ security/co-applicant answers; original 2023 Guidelines printed pp. 15–16

products.summary: Collateral-free household finance for consumption or personal needs, farm activities, food/agro processing and non-farm activities. benefits: Published maximum loan amount ₹1,00,000.

Classified as microfinance when the collateral-free household-income rule is met; the borrower deposit cannot be lien-marked and the loan cannot be secured by hypothecation.
The Bank's Fair Practice Code caps the household's total monthly loan repayments, including the proposed loan, at 50% of monthly household income.
eligibilityNotes: PNB's scheme sheet requires actual or projected annual household income up to ₹3,00,000. The FPC defines a household as husband, wife and their unmarried children.

When assessing the amount, PNB counts repayments on all outstanding household loans, including collateralized loans. Principal and interest repayments for existing loans and the proposed loan together must not exceed 50% of monthly household income; no new loan is provided while an existing household remains above that limit.

The FPC describes collateral-free microfinance loans irrespective of end use and physical/digital application or disbursal channel. The scheme sheet names personal/consumption, farm-based, food/agro-processing and non-farm purposes.

products.name: PNB PM SVANidhi Loan Scheme
customerSegments: Street vendors eligible under PM SVANidhi
products.summary: Collateral-free working-capital term finance for eligible street vendors. PNB publishes maximum amounts of ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000 for the first, second and third tranches, with 12-, 18- and 36-month tenures; the bank page quotes a starting RLLR-linked rate of 10.25% p.a.
benefits: Maximum loan caps rise by tranche: up to ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000; corresponding PNB tenures are 12, 18 and 36 months.
No collateral, no margin, and no processing or documentation fee on the PNB scheme page.
Eligible timely/early repayments can qualify the vendor for the next enhanced tranche; the Government FAQ also states a 7% p.a. interest subsidy for timely/early repayment.
Digital cashback is available on eligible inward/outward transactions and qualifying wholesale purchases, subject to separate caps and conditions.

The Government FAQ says a street vendor with a valid Letter of Recommendation (LoR) or Certificate of Vending (CoV) can apply through the scheme portal, mobile app or Urban Local Body assistance; it describes vendors of goods or public-facing services in streets/footpaths and similar places.
PNB assesses the requested limit within the scheme cap for each tranche; timely or early repayment qualifies the vendor for the next enhanced tranche.
requiredDocuments: A valid LoR or CoV is an application route stated in the Government FAQ; PNB's reviewed product page does not publish an exhaustive bank-specific document checklist.

customerSegments: EWS, LIG and MIG beneficiary families in urban areas without a pucca house anywhere in India
products.summary: Home finance for eligible urban households to purchase, re-purchase or construct a house under PMAY-U 2.0. The scheme publishes finance up to ₹25 lakh and an interest subsidy of up to ₹1.80 lakh, subject to income, property and tenure conditions.
benefits: Home loan up to ₹25 lakh, subject to LTV and repayment capacity
4% subsidy on the first ₹8 lakh of eligible principal, capped at ₹1.80 lakh and released in five annual instalments
Eligible property value up to ₹35 lakh and carpet area up to 120 sq m
15% margin for loans up to ₹25 lakh
Repayment up to 30 years or until age 70, whichever is earlier
eligibilityNotes: For urban EWS, LIG and MIG beneficiary families: annual household income up to ₹3 lakh, above ₹3 lakh to ₹6 lakh, and above ₹6 lakh to ₹9 lakh respectively; States/UTs may revise the EWS ceiling with Ministry concurrence.

Beneficiary family means husband, wife and unmarried children. No family member may own a pucca house anywhere in India, and the family must not have received a government housing allotment in the preceding 20 years.

House title is ordinarily in the adult female head's name or jointly with the spouse. Published exceptions apply where the family has no adult woman, including widower, unmarried, separated and transgender applicants.
Applicable to eligible purchase, re-purchase or construction loans sanctioned and disbursed on or after 1 September 2024; loan remains subject to PNB appraisal, LTV and repayment capacity.
requiredDocuments: For the housing loan: PNB's House Loan checklist asks for a completed application with photograph; identity, address, age, education and income proof; borrower-type-specific income records; and property papers matching purchase/construction purpose. Local/case-specific additions may apply.

For PMAY-U 2.0 Interest Subsidy Scheme beneficiary processing: Aadhaar or Aadhaar Virtual ID for each eligible beneficiary; household-income and no-pucca-house undertaking/declaration; and, as applicable, identity proof (Aadhaar/PAN), address proof and income certificate. MoHUA or the lending institution may request additional supporting documents.

customerSegments: Resident Indian senior citizens aged 60 or above who own a self-occupied residential house or flat

products.summary: A reverse-mortgage facility that pays regular monthly instalments against an unencumbered self-occupied home, up to ₹1 crore including interest, for senior-citizen living expenses.
benefits: No minimum income requirement; PNB bases the qualifying amount on the realizable value of the self-acquired, self-occupied home after a 20% margin.
Fixed monthly reverse-annuity payments for a selected 10–20-year tenor, or until the last surviving spouse dies, whichever comes first.
Maximum qualifying loan including interest: ₹1 crore; a medical-treatment lump sum for the senior citizen, spouse or dependent is capped at ₹15 lakh.

Borrower may prepay at any time. Legal heirs may settle the outstanding loan and accumulated interest without selling the property; repayment becomes due six months after the last surviving spouse's death.
eligibilityNotes: Applicant must be an Indian resident and an owner of a residential house/flat, aged 60 or above. For a joint spouse application, one spouse must be at least 60 and the other at least 58; title must be clear and in the applicant(s)' name(s).

The PNB 1193 (R1) undertaking further describes the property as self-acquired, self-occupied, unencumbered and not ancestral, used as the applicant(s)' permanent primary residence; it also asks applicants to confirm no more than one surviving legal spouse and no prior default with PNB or another financial institution.
requiredDocuments: PNB's Reverse Mortgage checklist lists a completed loan application with photograph, papers for the property to be mortgaged, a declaration/undertaking, co-borrower details if any, and Life Certificate-VII. PNB may ask for other documents required by the case.

facts.value: Indian-resident owner aged 60+; joint spouse may be 58+ if the other spouse is 60+. products.summary: Finance for new or used private-use cars, with separate new/old rate bands, an income-linked limit and up to 84 EMIs for a new vehicle.

image.alt: PNB Car Loan official artwork showing a car, handshake and coins

benefits: Individuals/proprietorships may borrow up to 25 times gross monthly income, capped at ₹1 crore
New-car rates vary by CIBIL band and EV status; used-car bands are separate
New-car repayment up to 84 EMIs; used-car repayment up to 60 EMIs
Floating-rate prepayment carries no charge; fixed-rate prepayment is 2% subject to published exceptions
eligibilityNotes: Individuals may apply singly or jointly; eligible company/firm borrowers must have been in cash profit for the preceding 2 years. Minimum net monthly salary/pension/income is ₹25,000, waived with 110% liquid term-deposit security. The 25×/₹1 crore limit applies to individuals/proprietorships; margins, co-borrower and security rules vary by route.
requiredDocuments: PNB's general vehicle-loan checklist lists a completed application form with recent photograph.

Salaried applicant: latest employer-issued salary certificate showing gross and net salary; income-tax return/Form 16 for the last two years, as applicable; salary-account statements for the last 6 or 12 months, as applicable.
Business concern: firm/company income-tax returns and audited balance sheet for the last two years.
Agriculturists and applicants engaged in allied agricultural activities: land-holding and cropping-pattern records or other proof of income.
Age proof and address proof.
New car/van/jeep: quotation from an authorised dealer for the vehicle to be purchased.

Used car/van/jeep: vehicle particulars and a registration-certificate copy (original to be produced at disbursement); latest authorised-dealer quotation; seller-purchaser agreement; seller-executed prescribed transfer form for the Regional Transport Office; and receipt showing up-to-date road tax/other taxes.
Proof of income of spouse, parents or earning children only where that income is considered to determine the loan amount.
Guarantor details with supporting papers and photograph, if applicable.
Statement of assets and liabilities with supporting documents.
PNB may require any other document or paper needed for the case; the checklist states that documents are obtained according to case requirements.

facts.label: Interest calculation and rate resets
facts.value: The sanctioned rate may be fixed or floating. Interest is calculated on the daily balance and charged monthly. For a floating RLLR-linked loan, a Reserve Bank repo-rate change updates RLLR from the next working day; the Mark-Up plus BSP component resets every three years from account opening, or at another interval allowed by bank/RBI rules.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Rate type and reset are as sanctioned; interest uses daily balance/monthly rests; RLLR changes from the next working day after a repo change and Mark-Up+BSP normally resets every three years.

facts.label: Fixed/floating rate switch
facts.value: On a benchmark-rate change, an EMI-based personal-loan borrower may switch between floating and fixed rates at most once during the loan term. The published switching charge is 0.50% of the outstanding loan or ₹10,000, whichever is lower, plus applicable GST.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Switching is offered at benchmark change, once in the full tenor; the stated fee is the lower of 0.50% of outstanding or ₹10,000, with GST.

facts.label: Options after a floating-rate increase
facts.value: If a repo-rate change alters the instalment, the borrower may choose a higher EMI, a longer term, or both within the scheme limit, or may partly/fully prepay. If no choice is made, PNB’s stated sequence is to extend the term within age limits first, then increase EMI, then use both if needed. Term extension is unavailable while the account is irregular or classified SMA-0/SMA-1/SMA-2/NPA.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower chooses EMI, tenor, both, or prepayment; PNB describes its default sequence and excludes irregular/SMA/NPA accounts from tenor extension.

facts.label: Other fees and event-based charges
facts.value: Fees specified in the sanction, including applicable upfront, processing, documentation and inspection charges, are collected before credit release. Event-based legal/valuation, cheque or NACH/SI dishonour, credit-information-report and CERSAI charges are recovered when the event occurs. The MITC says the paid processing/upfront fee is non-refundable.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Sanctioned charges are collected before release; event-based charges arise on the relevant event; paid upfront/processing fees are non-refundable.

facts.label: Repayment and first due date
facts.value: Repayment is by EMI unless the sanction says otherwise. The application form states that the first EMI/interest due date must be within 30 days of account opening. An EMI or interest amount unpaid on its due date is a default and may affect the borrower’s credit record.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 2, application form; PDF page 8, MITC §§6.6–7
facts.quoteOrContext: First EMI/interest is due no later than 30 days after account opening; repayment otherwise follows the sanction.

facts.label: Security and insurance conditions
facts.value: Primary security, collateral and any personal guarantee are as specified in the sanction. Assets mortgaged, hypothecated or charged to PNB must be insured against all risks at the borrower’s cost with the usual bank clause; if the borrower does not arrange it, PNB may insure and recover the cost. The borrower may opt for life and/or health cover with PNB as sole beneficiary.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Security/guarantee follow the sanction; charged assets must be insured by the borrower, and optional life/health cover may name PNB as sole beneficiary.

facts.label: Before loan disbursement
facts.value: Before disbursement, the borrower must provide sanction-letter/loan-agreement documents and execute the required loan and security documents. A written disbursement request is required. PNB says payment will preferably go directly to the seller; original bills/cash memos and necessary approvals must be provided, and the funds must be used for the sanctioned purpose.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Disbursement needs documents, executed security paperwork and written request; seller payment is preferred and use is restricted to the sanctioned purpose.

facts.label: Salary-credit and repayment instructions
facts.value: For salaried borrowers, the sanctioned amount is disbursed through the salary-credit account. The borrower must authorise salary deductions for instalments and undertake not to move the salary account to another bank during the loan. Non-salaried borrowers receive disbursement through their operative account.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The scheme clause differentiates salary-credit disbursement for employees from operative-account disbursement for non-salaried borrowers and requires salary deduction authority.

facts.label: Sanction validity
facts.value: A sanction remains valid for six months. Any sanctioned facility not availed within that period lapses; PNB also reserves the right to withdraw all or part of the sanction earlier.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Unavailed sanctioned facilities lapse after six months, subject to PNB’s stated earlier-withdrawal right.

facts.label: Late payment, credit reporting and collections
facts.value: The borrower remains responsible for paying each instalment on time. PNB says it reports account information monthly to CIBIL or another licensed credit-information company. On missed payments, it may contact the borrower by phone, SMS, post, electronic message or authorised personal visit and recover the cost of those communications/visits; legal recovery is subject to applicable law and prior notice where stated.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower must pay on time; credit data is reported monthly; recovery communications and visits may incur recoverable costs.

facts.label: Loan-record service timelines
facts.value: On request through a branch, PNB states that copies of loan documents can be provided within seven working days (an administrative fee applies) and a loan-account statement within three working days.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF gives seven working days for copies of loan documents and three working days for an account statement.

facts.label: Grievance escalation
facts.value: If a grievance remains unresolved for more than 15 days, the borrower may escalate it to PNB’s Principal Nodal Officer using the bank’s stated channels.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The published escalation point is after more than 15 days without resolution.

facts.label: Information requested in the application
facts.value: The form requests applicant/co-applicant personal and employment details, income and bank-account information, existing borrowing and monthly repayments, assets/liabilities, proposed collateral and guarantor details where applicable. Self-employed/professional applicants enter income for the previous three financial years. The acknowledgement leaves its acceptance/rejection notice period blank; this form does not give a numeric decision timeline. Supporting papers must be signed, and borrowers/guarantors sign all form pages including the MITC.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF pages 1–4, applicant/co-applicant form, acknowledgement and Part II guarantor form
facts.quoteOrContext: The application collects identity, employment, income, existing-credit, balance-sheet, collateral and conditional guarantor details; its acknowledgement uses an unfilled day-count blank.

facts.label: Prepayment when transferring the loan
facts.value: PNB 1114 states a 2% charge on prepaid outstanding for takeover of term loans only; it excludes non-fund-based facilities, working-capital limits and overdrafts. Its listed waivers include MSE borrowers; floating-rate non-business term loans to individuals; microfinance loans other than loans to NBFC-MFIs; fixed-rate loans switched to floating at reset; prepayment from the borrower’s own sources; transfer within 30 days after an upward spread/term circular; and benchmark-reset increases notified within 30 days and transferred within 90 days. This is a conditional takeover clause, not a universal charge. The product-specific pages’ NIL/own-source wording remains visible; confirm any fixed-rate takeover case with PNB.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF scopes 2% to term-loan takeover and lists seven borrower/transaction exemptions; other facilities are excluded.

facts.label: Penal charges for default and non-compliance
facts.value: PNB 1114 sets 2.00% p.a. on the amount of a single repayment-default/overdraft-irregularity trigger, or 3.00% p.a. for two or more such triggers. Missing review/renewal papers, failure to create/perfect security, or other sanction non-compliance attracts 2.00% p.a. on total outstanding. If both trigger groups apply, the total is capped at 4.00% p.a. (2.00% on default/irregularity plus 2.00% on outstanding). Exemptions: advances up to ₹25,000 and advances against deposits, life policies, government securities or gold within available security value. The 7-day cure provision is specifically for overdraft irregularity.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF gives separate rates/bases for repayment/OD events and sanction non-compliance, a combined cap, and specified exemptions.

products.summary: A housing loan for salaried Gen-Next borrowers aged up to 40, with a ₹35,000 minimum net monthly salary, 30-year repayment and need-based finance.

image.alt: PNB Gen-Next Housing Loan official artwork showing hands protecting a house

benefits: Minimum net monthly salary ₹35,000
Minimum loan ₹20 lakh; maximum is need-based subject to LTV and repayment capacity
1.25 times the regular housing-loan eligibility calculation, subject to prescribed LTV
Flat 30-year repayment period

Mandatory term insurance at least equal to the loan amount
eligibilityNotes: All salaried employees need at least three years' experience and salaried co-borrowers. One income-counted borrower must be no older than 40; other income-counted borrowers may be up to 45.
requiredDocuments: PNB's current general House Loan checklist is the applicant-document list reviewed for Gen-Next; the product page does not provide a separate checklist. It asks for the completed PNB form with photograph; identity, residence, age, education and income proof; borrower-type-specific salary/business/agricultural income records; and family income evidence only when counted toward the loan amount.

Property papers depend on the transaction: vendor title and approved plan; sale/allotment agreement and receipts; qualified engineer/architect estimate for construction/repair; applicable leasehold authority and non-encumbrance proof; or builder/society papers such as allotment/brochure, payment receipts, NOC and share/transfer papers.
PNB lists a supported assets/liabilities statement and any case-specific documents; the checklist is suggestive and local requirements may add to it.

customerSegments: Salaried employees
Professionals

products.summary: Housing finance for construction, purchase, plot purchase, additions, repairs, renovation and furnishing, with limits, margins and repayment periods varying by purpose.

image.alt: PNB Housing Loan for Public artwork showing a house held with its keys

benefits: Need-based finance for construction, additions and home/flat purchase, subject to project cost and repayment capacity.
Plot purchase and repairs/renovation/alterations each have a published ₹1 crore ceiling; furnishing is limited to 25% of the home loan or ₹1 crore, whichever is lower, within LTV.
Repayment up to 30 years for ordinary housing purposes; up to 15 years for repairs, renovation or alterations, each including any moratorium.
The current PNB UTSAV FESTIVITIES 2026 campaign waives home-loan upfront/processing and documentation charges through 31-12-2026.
eligibilityNotes: Individuals or co-borrowers with an assured regular income; the page lists salaried employees, professionals, self-employed people, business owners and farmers. PNB staff are also eligible under the public scheme.
Spouse, earning children and joint owners may have income clubbed if made co-borrowers; parents may co-borrow and have income clubbed in the stated son/daughter property-title cases.

The scheme page's up-to-₹30 lakh margin row is 20%/10%; the 10% route carries a higher card rate, which the borrower must be told before sanction. PNB's older general FAQ differs at 15%/20%; the product-specific April 2026 scheme page is used here.
requiredDocuments: Application and borrower evidence: completed PNB loan form with photograph; identity, address/residence, age, educational-qualification and income proof. If spouse, earning children or parents' income is used to determine the loan amount, provide that income evidence too.

Income route: salaried applicants — latest employer salary certificate showing gross and net salary, ITR/Form 16 for the last 2 years where applicable, and salary-account statements for the last 6 or 12 months as applicable; agriculturists — landholding and cropping-pattern records or other income proof; other individuals — ITRs and audited balance sheets for the previous 2 years where applicable, plus account statements for the last 6 or 12 months as applicable.

Property papers depend on purpose: built house from an individual — vendor title, approved plan, completion certificate if obtained, sale agreement/payment receipts, lease-transfer authority if relevant and non-encumbrance certificate; plot — vendor title, agreement/payment receipts, lease authority if relevant and non-encumbrance certificate; construction/repair/renovation — sale/lease deed, approved plan for construction/addition/alteration, qualified engineer/architect estimate, lease authority if relevant and non-encumbrance certificate; builder/authority/society purchase — sale agreement/allotment/brochure and correspondence, payment receipts, lease authority if relevant, and applicable society NOC/share/transfer papers; leasehold purchase through Power of Attorney — title and possession proof, agreement/payment receipts, non-encumbrance certificate, vendor Power of Attorney and Will, and awareness-cum-possession letter.
PNB also lists an assets-and-liabilities statement with supporting papers and any case-specific documents. The checklist is suggestive; local requirements may add documents.

benefits: Purpose includes acquisition, construction, repairs, renovation or improvement of a home, purchase of a plot and purchase of an under-construction home from the listed public/private bodies.
June 2026 terms allow up to 30 years including moratorium and use of remittances, specified Indian NRI accounts, rental income or permitted direct repayment by close relatives in India.
For repairs/renovation/alterations, the June 2026 bulletin publishes a maximum of ₹50 lakh.

The NRI scheme page and June bulletin do not state a numeric minimum income. Loan amount is need-based on project cost and repayment capacity.

Employed overseas: employer ID, valid work permit and employer contract. Self-employed: attested business-address proof.

Salaried: latest 12-month salary certificate and 12-month salary-account statement; the last-month salary certificate is to be attested. Other than salaried: last 2 years' audited/CA-certified balance sheet, profit-and-loss accounts and computation sheets where applicable, plus 12-month account statement; listed financial papers require attestation.

customerSegments: Indian nationals admitted to eligible NSQF or non-NSQF skill courses on the Skill India Digital Hub
products.summary: Skill-development loan for eligible vocational courses, with finance from ₹5,000 to ₹7.50 lakh, no collateral or third-party guarantee, and repayment up to 3, 5 or 7 years by loan amount. PNB's product page is dated 17 February 2025; current rates and charges were separately checked on PNB pages dated October 2026.
benefits: Eligible course expenses include tuition/course fees, examination/library/laboratory fees, caution deposit, books, equipment/instruments and other reasonable expenses necessary to complete the course.
PNB margin: nil up to ₹4 lakh; 5% above ₹4 lakh. Scholarship or assistantship is included in the student contribution; contribution may be brought pro rata year-to-year.
No collateral security or third-party guarantee is required under the published PNB scheme terms.
Repayment ceiling is 3 years for loans up to ₹50,000, 5 years for ₹50,000–₹1 lakh and 7 years above ₹1 lakh–₹7.50 lakh. PNB's published bands overlap at ₹50,000; no boundary rule is inferred.
Moratorium after course completion: 6 months for a course of up to one year; 12 months for a longer course.

PNB currently lists 9.85% p.a. floating for the published CGFSSD-covered route and 9.35% p.a. for the female-student route, with the stated RLLR+BSP spreads. Current fee schedule lists nil processing/upfront and documentation charges; prepayment charge is nil.

Under the NCGTC scheme, guarantee coverage is 75% of amount in default for covered loans up to ₹4 lakh and 70% above ₹4 lakh to ₹7.50 lakh. This is lender-side guarantee cover, not a cash benefit paid to the borrower.
eligibilityNotes: Applicant must be an Indian national, meet the course's minimum educational qualification and have secured admission to an eligible NSQF or non-NSQF course offered by a training entity onboarded on the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship's Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH).
A parent or guardian joins as co-borrower. If the student is a minor, the parent/guardian executes loan documents; the student accepts or ratifies them on attaining majority under the scheme FAQ.
The official product page publishes no minimum-income threshold. The itemized form/document checklist could not be retrieved and is not guessed.

facts.label: How the KCC limit is built from 1 January 2027
facts.value: For crop working capital, the season's State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area is increased by 10% for post-harvest/household needs and 20% for farm-asset maintenance, soil testing and listed advisory/technology services; applicable insurance premiums are added. The bank assesses the long-term investment component separately. The applicable State/District scale, crop, area, bank assessment and sanction determine the actual limit.

facts.quoteOrContext: The notification states a crop-base formula plus the two percentage components, adds premiums if any, fixes a marginal-farmer Flexi KCC range, and rounds the KCC limit to the nearest ₹1,000. The bank's sanctioned amount remains borrower- and season-specific.

facts.label: Collateral and optional insurance from 1 January 2027
facts.value: RBI directs commercial banks to waive collateral security and margin on agricultural loans, including allied-activity loans, up to ₹2 lakh per borrower. Above ₹2 lakh, the bank applies its policy and RBI rules; a bank may waive collateral up to ₹3 lakh for crop/stock-hypothecation loans with recovery tie-up. Crop, asset, accident and health insurance are optional; premium may be paid through KCC only with the farmer's explicit application-stage consent. Insurance financed under KCC is assigned to the lending bank.

facts.pageOrSection: Paragraphs 23–25 and 32–33; applicable to KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027

products.name: PNB my Property Loan
customerSegments: Individuals and joint owners with eligible immovable property
Salaried and non-salaried applicants
products.summary: A term loan or overdraft for personal purposes against eligible immovable property, from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 crore. PNB assesses the facility against both property value and repayment capacity; published term-loan rates vary by security, CIC band and tenure.
benefits: ₹2 lakh minimum and ₹5 crore maximum facility
Term loan or reducing-drawing-power overdraft
Finance assessment uses 65% of realizable property value or 36× eligible gross monthly income, whichever is lower
Term loan up to 180 months; overdraft liquidation up to 15 years, both subject to repayment by age 70
Nil prepayment charge on the reviewed scheme page
eligibilityNotes: Individuals and joint owners may apply if they have sufficient income and eligible immovable property to mortgage. Minimum net income: ₹25,000 per month for salaried applicants or ₹3 lakh per year for applicants other than salaried.
The property must be non-encumbered, built-up and self-occupied, with at least 25 years of residual life; PNB specifies an equitable or registered mortgage.
The purpose must be personal. PNB excludes speculative use, investment in a real-estate business and purposes prohibited by law.
Repayment-capacity limits include proposed instalments and existing debt obligations; statutory deductions are excluded from that calculation.
requiredDocuments: PNB application form with photograph; age proof; address proof; and income evidence.
Salaried: latest salary slip, ITR/Form 16 for the last 3 years, and the salary-credit account statement for the last 6 months.
Non-salaried: ITRs for the last 3 years and the last 6 months of the account statement showing regular business-income credits.
Income proof for spouse, parents or earning children if their income is used for loan amount or repayment-capacity assessment.
Documents for the immovable property proposed to be mortgaged; statement of assets and liabilities with supporting documents.
PNB describes this checklist as suggestive; local requirements and case-specific additional documents may apply.

facts.label: Borrower eligibility
facts.value: Individuals and joint owners with immovable property to mortgage and sufficient income to repay. Minimum net monthly salary is ₹25,000 for salaried applicants; minimum net annual income is ₹3 lakh for other applicants.

facts.label: Loan purpose
facts.value: Personal purposes are permitted except speculation. PNB excludes investment in a real-estate business, speculation in stocks, shares, securities, commodities or bullion, and purposes prohibited by law.

facts.label: Loan assessment
facts.value: The assessed amount is the lower of 65% of the property's realizable value and 36 times qualifying gross monthly income. For salaried applicants, PNB uses the latest salary certificate; for other applicants, it uses average gross monthly income over the last three years as reported in the last three ITRs.
facts.documentTitle: PNB my Property Loan — current Loan Against Mortgage page
facts.quoteOrContext: The page separates salaried assessment based on the latest salary certificate from non-salaried assessment using average income across the last three ITR years; each is compared with 65% of realizable property value.

facts.label: Repayment-capacity test
facts.value: Maximum permissible deductions are 60% of gross monthly total salary/income up to ₹1 lakh and 70% above ₹1 lakh. The ceiling includes the proposed mortgage instalment, existing deductions other than statutory deductions, loan instalments, actual term-loan interest and notional interest on the full sanctioned cash-credit/overdraft limit. PNB says repayment capacity uses the latest salary slips for salaried applicants and the three-year ITR average for others; income regularity is supported by salary slips, three-year ITRs/Form 16 or balance sheets, audited where stipulated.
