facts.label: Interest calculation and rate resets
facts.value: The sanctioned rate may be fixed or floating. Interest is calculated on the daily balance and charged monthly. For a floating RLLR-linked loan, a Reserve Bank repo-rate change updates RLLR from the next working day; the Mark-Up plus BSP component resets every three years from account opening, or at another interval allowed by bank/RBI rules.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Rate type and reset are as sanctioned; interest uses daily balance/monthly rests; RLLR changes from the next working day after a repo change and Mark-Up+BSP normally resets every three years.

facts.label: Fixed/floating rate switch
facts.value: On a benchmark-rate change, an EMI-based personal-loan borrower may switch between floating and fixed rates at most once during the loan term. The published switching charge is 0.50% of the outstanding loan or ₹10,000, whichever is lower, plus applicable GST.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Switching is offered at benchmark change, once in the full tenor; the stated fee is the lower of 0.50% of outstanding or ₹10,000, with GST.

facts.label: Options after a floating-rate increase
facts.value: If a repo-rate change alters the instalment, the borrower may choose a higher EMI, a longer term, or both within the scheme limit, or may partly/fully prepay. If no choice is made, PNB’s stated sequence is to extend the term within age limits first, then increase EMI, then use both if needed. Term extension is unavailable while the account is irregular or classified SMA-0/SMA-1/SMA-2/NPA.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower chooses EMI, tenor, both, or prepayment; PNB describes its default sequence and excludes irregular/SMA/NPA accounts from tenor extension.

facts.label: Other fees and event-based charges
facts.value: Fees specified in the sanction, including applicable upfront, processing, documentation and inspection charges, are collected before credit release. Event-based legal/valuation, cheque or NACH/SI dishonour, credit-information-report and CERSAI charges are recovered when the event occurs. The MITC says the paid processing/upfront fee is non-refundable.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Sanctioned charges are collected before release; event-based charges arise on the relevant event; paid upfront/processing fees are non-refundable.

facts.label: Repayment and first due date
facts.value: Repayment is by EMI unless the sanction says otherwise. The application form states that the first EMI/interest due date must be within 30 days of account opening. An EMI or interest amount unpaid on its due date is a default and may affect the borrower’s credit record.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 2, application form; PDF page 8, MITC §§6.6–7
facts.quoteOrContext: First EMI/interest is due no later than 30 days after account opening; repayment otherwise follows the sanction.

facts.label: Security and insurance conditions
facts.value: Primary security, collateral and any personal guarantee are as specified in the sanction. Assets mortgaged, hypothecated or charged to PNB must be insured against all risks at the borrower’s cost with the usual bank clause; if the borrower does not arrange it, PNB may insure and recover the cost. The borrower may opt for life and/or health cover with PNB as sole beneficiary.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Security/guarantee follow the sanction; charged assets must be insured by the borrower, and optional life/health cover may name PNB as sole beneficiary.

facts.label: Before loan disbursement
facts.value: Before disbursement, the borrower must provide sanction-letter/loan-agreement documents and execute the required loan and security documents. A written disbursement request is required. PNB says payment will preferably go directly to the seller; original bills/cash memos and necessary approvals must be provided, and the funds must be used for the sanctioned purpose.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Disbursement needs documents, executed security paperwork and written request; seller payment is preferred and use is restricted to the sanctioned purpose.

facts.label: Salary-credit and repayment instructions
facts.value: For salaried borrowers, the sanctioned amount is disbursed through the salary-credit account. The borrower must authorise salary deductions for instalments and undertake not to move the salary account to another bank during the loan. Non-salaried borrowers receive disbursement through their operative account.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The scheme clause differentiates salary-credit disbursement for employees from operative-account disbursement for non-salaried borrowers and requires salary deduction authority.

facts.label: Sanction validity
facts.value: A sanction remains valid for six months. Any sanctioned facility not availed within that period lapses; PNB also reserves the right to withdraw all or part of the sanction earlier.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Unavailed sanctioned facilities lapse after six months, subject to PNB’s stated earlier-withdrawal right.

facts.label: Late payment, credit reporting and collections
facts.value: The borrower remains responsible for paying each instalment on time. PNB says it reports account information monthly to CIBIL or another licensed credit-information company. On missed payments, it may contact the borrower by phone, SMS, post, electronic message or authorised personal visit and recover the cost of those communications/visits; legal recovery is subject to applicable law and prior notice where stated.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower must pay on time; credit data is reported monthly; recovery communications and visits may incur recoverable costs.

facts.label: Loan-record service timelines
facts.value: On request through a branch, PNB states that copies of loan documents can be provided within seven working days (an administrative fee applies) and a loan-account statement within three working days.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions

facts.label: Interest calculation and rate resets
facts.value: The sanctioned rate may be fixed or floating. Interest is calculated on the daily balance and charged monthly. For a floating RLLR-linked loan, a Reserve Bank repo-rate change updates RLLR from the next working day; the Mark-Up plus BSP component resets every three years from account opening, or at another interval allowed by bank/RBI rules.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Rate type and reset are as sanctioned; interest uses daily balance/monthly rests; RLLR changes from the next working day after a repo change and Mark-Up+BSP normally resets every three years.

facts.label: Fixed/floating rate switch
facts.value: On a benchmark-rate change, an EMI-based personal-loan borrower may switch between floating and fixed rates at most once during the loan term. The published switching charge is 0.50% of the outstanding loan or ₹10,000, whichever is lower, plus applicable GST.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Switching is offered at benchmark change, once in the full tenor; the stated fee is the lower of 0.50% of outstanding or ₹10,000, with GST.

facts.label: Options after a floating-rate increase
facts.value: If a repo-rate change alters the instalment, the borrower may choose a higher EMI, a longer term, or both within the scheme limit, or may partly/fully prepay. If no choice is made, PNB’s stated sequence is to extend the term within age limits first, then increase EMI, then use both if needed. Term extension is unavailable while the account is irregular or classified SMA-0/SMA-1/SMA-2/NPA.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower chooses EMI, tenor, both, or prepayment; PNB describes its default sequence and excludes irregular/SMA/NPA accounts from tenor extension.

facts.label: Other fees and event-based charges
facts.value: Fees specified in the sanction, including applicable upfront, processing, documentation and inspection charges, are collected before credit release. Event-based legal/valuation, cheque or NACH/SI dishonour, credit-information-report and CERSAI charges are recovered when the event occurs. The MITC says the paid processing/upfront fee is non-refundable.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Sanctioned charges are collected before release; event-based charges arise on the relevant event; paid upfront/processing fees are non-refundable.

facts.label: Repayment and first due date
facts.value: Repayment is by EMI unless the sanction says otherwise. The application form states that the first EMI/interest due date must be within 30 days of account opening. An EMI or interest amount unpaid on its due date is a default and may affect the borrower’s credit record.

facts.label: Security and insurance conditions

Assets mortgaged, hypothecated or charged to PNB must be insured against all risks at the borrower’s cost with the usual bank clause; if the borrower does not arrange it, PNB may insure and recover the cost. The borrower may opt for life and/or health cover with PNB as sole beneficiary.

facts.quoteOrContext: Security/guarantee follow the sanction; charged assets must be insured by the borrower, and optional life/health cover may name PNB as sole beneficiary.

facts.label: Before loan disbursement
facts.value: Before disbursement, the borrower must provide sanction-letter/loan-agreement documents and execute the required loan and security documents. A written disbursement request is required. PNB says payment will preferably go directly to the seller; original bills/cash memos and necessary approvals must be provided, and the funds must be used for the sanctioned purpose.

facts.label: Salary-credit and repayment instructions

The borrower must authorise salary deductions for instalments and undertake not to move the salary account to another bank during the loan. Non-salaried borrowers receive disbursement through their operative account.

facts.quoteOrContext: The scheme clause differentiates salary-credit disbursement for employees from operative-account disbursement for non-salaried borrowers and requires salary deduction authority.

facts.label: Sanction validity
facts.value: A sanction remains valid for six months. Any sanctioned facility not availed within that period lapses; PNB also reserves the right to withdraw all or part of the sanction earlier.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Unavailed sanctioned facilities lapse after six months, subject to PNB’s stated earlier-withdrawal right.

eligibilityNotes: For children already identified under PM CARES for Children; new enrolment closed on 31 December 2021.

The published scheme covers children who lost both parents, a surviving parent or a legal/adoptive guardian to COVID-19 between 11 March 2020 and 31 December 2021, were under 18 on the date of death, are resident Indians and gained admission to a recognized Indian higher-education course through entrance/merit selection, subject to the page's stated postgraduate work-experience exception.
requiredDocuments: For an existing eligible PM CARES for Children beneficiary: PNB-format application, passport-size photo, KYC identity/address proof, age proof and PAN. If PAN is unavailable at sanction, obtain it before disbursement; student Aadhaar is required where applicable under PNB's stated rule.

Student/course: proof of passing the last qualifying examination, admission letter and course prospectus showing charges such as admission, examination and hostel fees; PNB may request other case- or purpose-specific papers.

Co-applicant/guarantor, where applicable: PNB-format application, photo, KYC identity/address and age proof, and PAN. If the co-applicant has an existing loan with another lender, provide its latest six-month account statement and sanction letter.

Conditional: income certificate from the designated State/UT authority, ITR, Form 16 or audited accounts only when required for a government interest-subsidy claim; title deed/proof of title only when immovable property is mortgaged as security. New PM CARES enrolment closed on 31 December 2021.

Co-applicant/guarantor, where applicable: PNB-format application, photo, KYC identity/address and age proof, and PAN. If the co-applicant has an existing loan with another lender, provide its latest six-month account statement and sanction letter.

Conditional: income certificate from the designated State/UT authority, ITR, Form 16 or audited accounts only when required for a government interest-subsidy claim; title deed/proof of title only when immovable property is mortgaged as security.

products.name: PNB Rooftop Solar Loan (PM Surya Ghar)
customerSegments: Individual residential-property owners with rooftop rights and a PNB savings account
products.summary: Finance for a new residential rooftop system up to 10 kW. PNB's current rate table shows 6.00% floating up to ₹2,00,000; above that through ₹6,00,000 it lists 7.50%–10.10% floating and 8.50%–11.10% fixed, by CIBIL band and PNB home-loan relationship. Maximum tenure is 10 years including a six-month moratorium.
benefits: Up to 3 kW: maximum loan ₹2,00,000; above 3 kW through 10 kW: maximum ₹6,00,000.
Current published rates: 6.00% p.a. floating up to ₹2,00,000; above that through ₹6,00,000, floating 7.50%–10.10% p.a. or fixed 8.50%–11.10% p.a., by score and PNB home-loan relationship.
MNRE residential subsidy: ₹30,000 at 1 kW, ₹60,000 at 2 kW, ₹78,000 at 3 kW and capped at ₹78,000 above 3 kW through 10 kW.
Six-month moratorium; maximum repayment period 10 years inclusive of moratorium; nil processing/upfront fee.
eligibilityNotes: Individual applicant alone or jointly with parents, spouse, earning children (married or unmarried) or an earning daughter-in-law; applicant(s) must have CIC/CIBIL TU 680 or equivalent, including −1/0/Nil/no-hit.

Applicant or co-applicant must own the residential property and rooftop rights, have sufficient roof area under MNRE requirements, and provide the latest electricity bill confirming property ownership. Applicant must hold a PNB savings account; maximum applicant age is 75.

For loans above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000: minimum annual income ₹3,00,000; all deductions including the proposed instalment must not exceed 50% of gross annual salary/income; regular income over the tenure must be established. No minimum income or income assessment is required up to ₹2,00,000.
requiredDocuments: Application form and sanction letter; KYC documents including Aadhaar and other applicable KYC records.
Latest electricity bill and proof of residential-property ownership (for example, tax receipt or sale deed); vendor quotation and the feasibility reports required by MNRE.
For loans above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000: minimum one-year ITR/Form 16 and the last six months' account statement. PAN is optional up to ₹2,00,000 and mandatory above ₹2,00,000.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Individuals may apply alone or jointly with parents, spouse, earning children (married or unmarried) or an earning daughter-in-law. Applicant(s) need CIC/CIBIL TU 680 or equivalent, including −1/0/Nil/no-hit; the applicant or co-applicant must own the home and rooftop rights, have MNRE-required roof area and a latest electricity bill confirming ownership. Applicant must hold a PNB savings account; maximum age 75.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: PNB lists permitted individual co-applicants, the credit-score rule, owner/roof/bill conditions, age 75 and mandatory PNB savings-account relationship.

facts.label: Borrower margin
facts.value: 10% for loan amounts up to ₹2,00,000; 20% for amounts above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: PNB sets 10% margin through ₹2 lakh and 20% above ₹2 lakh through ₹6 lakh.

facts.label: Income assessment
facts.value: For loans above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000, all deductions including the proposed instalment must not exceed 50% of gross annual salary/income; regular income over the full loan period must be established. PNB asks for at least one year of ITR/Form 16 and a six-month account statement. No income assessment is required up to ₹2,00,000.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.pageOrSection: Net Annual Income; Income Assessment; Regularity of Income
facts.quoteOrContext: The page applies the 50% deduction limit, income-regularity check and evidence documents only to the above-₹2 lakh-to-₹6 lakh loan band.

facts.label: Moratorium
facts.value: Six months from disbursement; accrued interest is payable as and when charged. The moratorium is included in the maximum 10-year repayment period.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: PNB states six months from disbursement and says interest is paid when charged.

facts.label: Required documents
facts.value: Application form and sanction letter; KYC including Aadhaar and other applicable KYC records; vendor quotation and MNRE-required feasibility reports; latest electricity bill; proof of residential-property ownership (such as tax receipt or sale deed). For loans above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000, provide at least one year of ITR/Form 16 and the last six months' account statement. PAN is optional through ₹2,00,000 and mandatory above ₹2,00,000.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.pageOrSection: Documents Required; Net Annual Income; Regularity of Income

facts.label: Disbursement
facts.value: Loan proceeds and the borrower's contribution are paid directly to the vendor/EPC contractor after MNRE-required feasibility reports are submitted. The borrower/vendor claims subsidy using the loan account number.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The page specifies direct payment to vendor/EPC after feasibility reports and subsidy claim with loan-account number.

facts.label: Priority-sector classification
facts.value: PNB classifies this rooftop-solar purchase loan under priority sector.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The bank states the solar-equipment loan is classified under priority sector.

facts.label: Vendor requirement
facts.value: Residential rooftop systems must be supplied by vendors empanelled under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)/state DISCOM vendor list.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: PNB says all residential systems must be sold by MNRE-empanelled vendors and links the statewise vendor list.

facts.label: Security
facts.value: Hypothecation of the equipment. Third-party guarantee is waived for loans up to ₹2,00,000. Above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000, PNB requires a third-party guarantee with net means at least equal to the loan amount.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The scheme differentiates guarantee requirements at ₹2 lakh and requires guarantor net means at least equal to the loan above that amount.

facts.label: MNRE subsidy
facts.value: ₹30,000 at 1 kW; ₹60,000 at 2 kW; ₹78,000 at 3 kW; for systems above 3 kW through 10 kW, subsidy is capped at ₹78,000 and credited to the loan account after a claim quoting the loan account number.
facts.documentTitle: PNB Scheme for Financing of Rooftop Solar Power Systems — current full-page review
facts.quoteOrContext: PNB publishes the four subsidy capacity tiers and ₹78,000 cap; claim is linked to the loan account.

facts.label: Equipment insurance
facts.value: Asset insurance is not mandatory up to ₹2,00,000. Above ₹2,00,000 through ₹6,00,000, the installation asset must be insured for its total cost when system capacity exceeds 3 kW; the customer pays the premium.

products.summary: PNB Sahyog is a personal-loan scheme for public borrowers and LIC agents. Eligibility and documents differ by route; its FAQ publishes location-based take-home thresholds, amount limits and repayment terms, while a separate rate matrix varies by borrower class and CIBIL band.
benefits: Up to 15 times gross monthly salary, maximum ₹10 lakh
Minimum take-home after deductions: ₹15,000 in metro/urban centres or ₹10,000 in semi-urban/rural centres
Nil margin
Repayment within remaining service or up to 60 EMIs
Partial or full prepayment from the borrower's own identifiable sources is permitted without penalty under PNB's Personal Loan FAQ
eligibilityNotes: Public applicants include permanent Central/State Government or PSU employees and employees of reputed companies/institutions using the PNB salary-account or employer check-off route.
For applicants using employer check-off, the personal-loan FAQ states at least 3 years of service including previous employers.
LIC-agent applicants must be under 60, have more than 5 years of agency, a steady source of income, and a PNB savings-fund account.
Minimum take-home after deductions is ₹15,000 in metro/urban centres or ₹10,000 in semi-urban/rural centres.
The FAQ requires a suitable guarantee acceptable to PNB; the LIC-agent checklist lists policy assignment or full-value tangible collateral as the security route.
requiredDocuments: Completed personal-loan application form with a recent photograph, plus age, education and official/residential address proof.
Public salaried route: latest salary certificate, employer-authenticated ITR/Form 16 for the last 2 years, and at least 1 year of statements from the salary-credit account.
LIC-agent route: 3 years of salary/ITR/Form 16 evidence, a 1-year statement for the account declared in the ITR, and agency number/code.
LIC-agent route: assignment of the applicant's LIC policy with sum assured equal to the loan, or tangible collateral worth 100% of the loan; provide the relevant policy/security and guarantee papers.

facts.label: Interest calculation and rate resets
facts.value: The sanctioned rate may be fixed or floating. Interest is calculated on the daily balance and charged monthly. For a floating RLLR-linked loan, a Reserve Bank repo-rate change updates RLLR from the next working day; the Mark-Up plus BSP component resets every three years from account opening, or at another interval allowed by bank/RBI rules.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Rate type and reset are as sanctioned; interest uses daily balance/monthly rests; RLLR changes from the next working day after a repo change and Mark-Up+BSP normally resets every three years.

facts.label: Fixed/floating rate switch
facts.value: On a benchmark-rate change, an EMI-based personal-loan borrower may switch between floating and fixed rates at most once during the loan term. The published switching charge is 0.50% of the outstanding loan or ₹10,000, whichever is lower, plus applicable GST.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Switching is offered at benchmark change, once in the full tenor; the stated fee is the lower of 0.50% of outstanding or ₹10,000, with GST.

facts.label: Options after a floating-rate increase
facts.value: If a repo-rate change alters the instalment, the borrower may choose a higher EMI, a longer term, or both within the scheme limit, or may partly/fully prepay. If no choice is made, PNB’s stated sequence is to extend the term within age limits first, then increase EMI, then use both if needed. Term extension is unavailable while the account is irregular or classified SMA-0/SMA-1/SMA-2/NPA.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower chooses EMI, tenor, both, or prepayment; PNB describes its default sequence and excludes irregular/SMA/NPA accounts from tenor extension.

facts.label: Other fees and event-based charges
facts.value: Fees specified in the sanction, including applicable upfront, processing, documentation and inspection charges, are collected before credit release. Event-based legal/valuation, cheque or NACH/SI dishonour, credit-information-report and CERSAI charges are recovered when the event occurs. The MITC says the paid processing/upfront fee is non-refundable.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Sanctioned charges are collected before release; event-based charges arise on the relevant event; paid upfront/processing fees are non-refundable.

facts.label: Repayment and first due date
facts.value: Repayment is by EMI unless the sanction says otherwise. The application form states that the first EMI/interest due date must be within 30 days of account opening. An EMI or interest amount unpaid on its due date is a default and may affect the borrower’s credit record.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 2, application form; PDF page 8, MITC §§6.6–7
facts.quoteOrContext: First EMI/interest is due no later than 30 days after account opening; repayment otherwise follows the sanction.

facts.label: Security and insurance conditions
facts.value: Primary security, collateral and any personal guarantee are as specified in the sanction. Assets mortgaged, hypothecated or charged to PNB must be insured against all risks at the borrower’s cost with the usual bank clause; if the borrower does not arrange it, PNB may insure and recover the cost. The borrower may opt for life and/or health cover with PNB as sole beneficiary.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Security/guarantee follow the sanction; charged assets must be insured by the borrower, and optional life/health cover may name PNB as sole beneficiary.

facts.label: Before loan disbursement
facts.value: Before disbursement, the borrower must provide sanction-letter/loan-agreement documents and execute the required loan and security documents. A written disbursement request is required. PNB says payment will preferably go directly to the seller; original bills/cash memos and necessary approvals must be provided, and the funds must be used for the sanctioned purpose.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Disbursement needs documents, executed security paperwork and written request; seller payment is preferred and use is restricted to the sanctioned purpose.

facts.label: Salary-credit and repayment instructions
facts.value: For salaried borrowers, the sanctioned amount is disbursed through the salary-credit account. The borrower must authorise salary deductions for instalments and undertake not to move the salary account to another bank during the loan. Non-salaried borrowers receive disbursement through their operative account.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The scheme clause differentiates salary-credit disbursement for employees from operative-account disbursement for non-salaried borrowers and requires salary deduction authority.

facts.label: Sanction validity
facts.value: A sanction remains valid for six months. Any sanctioned facility not availed within that period lapses; PNB also reserves the right to withdraw all or part of the sanction earlier.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: Unavailed sanctioned facilities lapse after six months, subject to PNB’s stated earlier-withdrawal right.

facts.label: Late payment, credit reporting and collections
facts.value: The borrower remains responsible for paying each instalment on time. PNB says it reports account information monthly to CIBIL or another licensed credit-information company. On missed payments, it may contact the borrower by phone, SMS, post, electronic message or authorised personal visit and recover the cost of those communications/visits; legal recovery is subject to applicable law and prior notice where stated.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The borrower must pay on time; credit data is reported monthly; recovery communications and visits may incur recoverable costs.

facts.label: Loan-record service timelines
facts.value: On request through a branch, PNB states that copies of loan documents can be provided within seven working days (an administrative fee applies) and a loan-account statement within three working days.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF gives seven working days for copies of loan documents and three working days for an account statement.

facts.label: Grievance escalation
facts.value: If a grievance remains unresolved for more than 15 days, the borrower may escalate it to PNB’s Principal Nodal Officer using the bank’s stated channels.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The published escalation point is after more than 15 days without resolution.

facts.label: Information requested in the application
facts.value: The form requests applicant/co-applicant personal and employment details, income and bank-account information, existing borrowing and monthly repayments, assets/liabilities, proposed collateral and guarantor details where applicable. Self-employed/professional applicants enter income for the previous three financial years. The acknowledgement leaves its acceptance/rejection notice period blank; this form does not give a numeric decision timeline. Supporting papers must be signed, and borrowers/guarantors sign all form pages including the MITC.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF pages 1–4, applicant/co-applicant form, acknowledgement and Part II guarantor form
facts.quoteOrContext: The application collects identity, employment, income, existing-credit, balance-sheet, collateral and conditional guarantor details; its acknowledgement uses an unfilled day-count blank.

facts.label: Prepayment when transferring the loan
facts.value: PNB 1114 states a 2% charge on prepaid outstanding for takeover of term loans only; it excludes non-fund-based facilities, working-capital limits and overdrafts. Its listed waivers include MSE borrowers; floating-rate non-business term loans to individuals; microfinance loans other than loans to NBFC-MFIs; fixed-rate loans switched to floating at reset; prepayment from the borrower’s own sources; transfer within 30 days after an upward spread/term circular; and benchmark-reset increases notified within 30 days and transferred within 90 days. This is a conditional takeover clause, not a universal charge. The product-specific pages’ NIL/own-source wording remains visible; confirm any fixed-rate takeover case with PNB.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF scopes 2% to term-loan takeover and lists seven borrower/transaction exemptions; other facilities are excluded.

facts.label: Penal charges for default and non-compliance
facts.value: PNB 1114 sets 2.00% p.a. on the amount of a single repayment-default/overdraft-irregularity trigger, or 3.00% p.a. for two or more such triggers. Missing review/renewal papers, failure to create/perfect security, or other sanction non-compliance attracts 2.00% p.a. on total outstanding. If both trigger groups apply, the total is capped at 4.00% p.a. (2.00% on default/irregularity plus 2.00% on outstanding). Exemptions: advances up to ₹25,000 and advances against deposits, life policies, government securities or gold within available security value. The 7-day cure provision is specifically for overdraft irregularity.
facts.documentTitle: PNB 1114 (R1) — Personal Loan application form and Most Important Terms & Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF gives separate rates/bases for repayment/OD events and sanction non-compliance, a combined cap, and specified exemptions.

customerSegments: Students pursuing higher education abroad
products.summary: Education finance for eligible higher-education courses abroad. PNB's product page and FAQ differ on whether the student must be resident in India; confirm residency eligibility with PNB if applying from abroad.
benefits: Need-based finance for eligible course expenses abroad
Nil margin up to ₹4 lakh; 15% above ₹4 lakh
No tangible security or third-party guarantee up to ₹7.50 lakh; suitable collateral is required above that amount
Repayment up to 15 years, with course period + 1 year moratorium
Studies-abroad processing fee: 1% of the loan, minimum ₹10,000, refundable after first disbursement
eligibilityNotes: PNB's product page says a resident Indian must gain admission after HSC (10+2) or equivalent through entrance-test or merit selection to a recognized higher-education course abroad.

PNB's FAQ separately says any Indian national can apply. Because that is broader than the product-page residency rule, applicants who are Indian nationals but not resident in India should confirm eligibility with PNB before applying.

A separate route may consider recognized/accredited diploma or certificate courses abroad other than aeronautical, pilot-training and shipping courses. The page requires liquid security worth 125% of the loan and evidence of family financial credentials for this route.
The FAQ lists parents, grandparents, spouse and parents-in-law as possible co-obligants.
requiredDocuments: Student: PNB-format application, passport-size photo, KYC identity/address proof, age proof and PAN. If PAN is unavailable at sanction, obtain it before disbursement; student Aadhaar is required where applicable under PNB's stated rule.

Student/course: proof of passing the last qualifying examination, admission letter and course prospectus showing charges such as admission, examination and hostel fees; PNB may request other case- or purpose-specific papers.

Co-applicant/guarantor, where applicable: PNB-format application, photo, KYC identity/address and age proof, and PAN. If the co-applicant has an existing loan with another lender, provide its latest six-month account statement and sanction letter.

Overseas-study and other conditional papers: passport and visa; provide the visa copy before first disbursement. Government-subsidy income evidence applies only when claiming a relevant scheme, and property title proof only if immovable property is mortgaged.

products.summary: SBI's general resident home loan for purchase, construction, takeover, plot plus construction, extension, repair or renovation, available as a term loan or overdraft with repayment up to 30 years.

facts.label: Eligible purposes
facts.value: Ready-built, under-construction or pre-owned home purchase; plot or plot plus construction; self-construction; extension; repair or renovation
facts.documentTitle: SBI General Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: The page presents these purposes within one general home-loan product.

facts.label: Maximum tenure
facts.value: 360 months, subject to repayment by age 70
facts.documentTitle: SBI General Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: Minimum application age is 18 and maximum repayment age is 70.

facts.label: Processing fee
facts.value: 0.35% of the loan amount; minimum ₹5,000. Maximum ₹15,000 for salaried customers or ₹18,000 for non-salaried customers, plus GST.
facts.unit: % of loan amount; minimum and applicant-type caps
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 4 (P3) — Fees and charges, salaried and non-salaried processing-fee rows
facts.quoteOrContext: The current MITC states 0.35% of loan amount with a ₹5,000 minimum, capped at ₹15,000 for salaried and ₹18,000 for non-salaried customers, plus GST. No effective date is printed; the document says charges may change.

facts.label: Prepayment penalty
facts.value: Nil
facts.documentTitle: SBI General Home Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: The current product page states no pre-payment penalty.

facts.label: Conversion, switchover and revalidation charges
facts.value: Term Loan to Maxgain or Maxgain to Term Loan conversion: ₹5,000 plus GST. Switchover from MCLR, SBAR or Base Rate to EBLR: ₹5,000 plus GST. Loan revalidation: ₹5,000 plus GST.

facts.value: Home loan
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — official product page

facts.label: Prepayment / pre-closure charge
facts.value: No prepayment or pre-closure penalty on floating-rate home loans, regardless of how long the account has run or the source of funds.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The no-penalty statement is expressly for floating-interest home loans and does not make a claim about any other rate type.

facts.label: APR
facts.value: Not published as a separate APR; SBI publishes the applicable interest/card-rate route, not an all-in annual percentage rate for this product page.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — official product page
facts.pageOrSection: Interest Rates & Fees; complete page review
facts.quoteOrContext: The page links to current card rates and lists interest-related features, but publishes no APR calculation or all-in annual percentage rate.

facts.label: Minimum income
facts.value: Not published as a rupee income threshold; the page specifies resident-borrower eligibility and requests income documents, but gives no salary or annual-income floor.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — official product page
facts.quoteOrContext: The complete page lists resident status, age 18–70 and required salary/Form 16 or tax-return documents, but no numeric minimum income.

facts.label: Maximum loan amount
facts.value: Not published as a fixed rupee cap on the reviewed product page; SBI sends applicants to its online eligibility/card-rate route for the sanctioned amount.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — official product page
facts.quoteOrContext: The complete page displays 'Loan Amount: Click Here' rather than a product-specific rupee ceiling; the linked application route determines eligibility.

facts.label: Maximum loan-to-value
facts.value: Up to 90% for loans up to ₹30 lakh; 80% above ₹30 lakh and up to ₹75 lakh; 75% above ₹75 lakh.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 1 (P0) — Loan to Value Ratio table
facts.quoteOrContext: The current table prints 90% up to ₹30 lakh, 80% above ₹30 lakh through ₹75 lakh and 75% above ₹75 lakh. This replaces the older reviewed ₹20-lakh threshold.

facts.label: Penal charges for irregularity
facts.value: 2.40% p.a. on the irregular amount for irregularity up to 60 days; 5% p.a. on the irregular amount when it continues beyond 60 days.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The current wording distinguishes irregularity up to 60 days at 2.40% p.a. from continuous irregularity beyond 60 days at 5% p.a., both on the irregular portion. This supersedes the older 2% after 30 days wording.

facts.label: Missed EMI / returned payment charges
facts.value: Missed EMI: ₹250 + GST per missed EMI; cheque returned for insufficient funds: ₹500 + GST; failed SI/NACH: ₹250 + GST per failure.
facts.unit: per missed EMI, returned cheque or failed mandate
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 5 (P4) — Failed or Non-payment EMI / Cheque returned / SI dishonours table
facts.quoteOrContext: The cheque-return amount is limited to insufficient-funds returns. The PDF says these rates may vary and fees/charges are subject to change.

facts.label: Fixed-rate option
facts.value: The MITC says no fixed-rate option is available at the time of the document; the home-loan interest is otherwise charged on a daily reducing balance with monthly rests at the prevailing floating rate.
facts.documentTitle: Most Important Terms and Conditions — SBI Home Loan
facts.pageOrSection: Page 1 — Rate of Interest and Calculation of Interest
facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC describes prevailing floating-rate charging and explicitly prints ‘No Fixed rate option is available now’.

facts.label: Primary security
facts.value: Equitable or registered mortgage/extension of mortgage over the financed land and building or flat. Where mortgage creation is delayed, SBI may require interim security, including a third-party guarantee; specified liquid securities may be pledged in lieu of mortgage where accepted.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 3 (P2) — Security, Collateral and Interim Security Pending Mortgage
facts.quoteOrContext: The primary security is the financed property; liquid securities or a third-party guarantee are conditional alternatives/interim arrangements, not a claim that collateral is always required.

facts.label: Property insurance
facts.value: The financed house/flat must be insured for actual project cost after deducting land, stamp duty and registration charges, against fire, riots, earthquake, lightning, flood and other applicable risks, in the joint names of borrower and SBI. The borrower pays the premium.

normalizedValue.insuredValueBasis: actual project cost less land, stamp duty and registration charges

facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.quoteOrContext: The PDF specifies the insured-value calculation, joint names and borrower-paid cost; it does not say this is a bank-sold insurance policy.

facts.label: Current EBLR benchmark
facts.value: EBLR 8.15% + CRP + BSP, effective 15 October 2026. The product- and borrower-specific CRP/BSP and final sanctioned rate are not shown in this shared benchmark table.
facts.documentTitle: SBI External Benchmark based Lending Rate — 15 October 2026 revision
facts.pageOrSection: EBLR/RLLR table; effective 15 October 2026; last updated 14 October 2026; home-loan portal benchmark-reset notification

facts.label: Maximum repayment period
facts.value: Up to 30 years or until the borrower reaches age 70, whichever comes first.

facts.quoteOrContext: The MITC sets a maximum 30-year tenor or full repayment by age 70, whichever is earlier; it separately allows repayment up to age 75 for Privilege and Shaurya Home Loans.

facts.value: 7.50% p.a. onwards from 15 October 2026; SBI marks the rate subject to terms and conditions. This is the Home Loans starting rate, not a full CIBIL/variant card range or an individual quote.

facts.quoteOrContext: The official rate page prints 7.50% p.a. onwards effective 15.10.2026 with terms applying, and the adjacent SEE PRODUCTS link is the SBI Home Loans portal. Do not extend this starting figure to individual variants or treat it as the full card range.

facts.label: Primary security
facts.value: Equitable or registered mortgage/extension of mortgage over the financed land and building or flat. Where mortgage creation is delayed, SBI may require interim security, including a third-party guarantee; specified liquid securities may be pledged in lieu of mortgage where accepted.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Home Loan — Most Important Terms and Conditions
facts.pageOrSection: PDF page 3 (P2) — Security, Collateral and Interim Security Pending Mortgage
facts.quoteOrContext: The primary security is the financed property; liquid securities or a third-party guarantee are conditional alternatives/interim arrangements, not a claim that collateral is always required.

facts.label: Property insurance
facts.value: The financed house/flat must be insured for actual project cost after deducting land, stamp duty and registration charges, against fire, riots, earthquake, lightning, flood and other applicable risks, in the joint names of borrower and SBI. The borrower pays the premium.

facts.label: APR

facts.label: Minimum income
facts.value: No numeric minimum income is published. SBI's NRI Home Loan checklist requires employment, salary and tax evidence for the applicant/co-applicant (including last three months' salary proof, six months' salary-credit statements and tax returns, with business financials for non-salaried applicants).

facts.label: Maximum repayment period
facts.value: Up to 30 years or until the borrower reaches age 70, whichever comes first.

products.name: SBI NRI Loan Against Deposits
customerSegments: NRE, NRO or FCNR(B) depositors seeking a secured demand loan, overdraft or eligible foreign-currency loan
products.summary: A secured facility for an SBI NRE, NRO or FCNR(B) depositor, available as a demand loan or overdraft and, against FCNR(B), also as an eligible foreign-currency loan.
products.geographicAvailability: NRO and NRE facilities through the home branch in India; FCNR(B)-backed facilities through designated Indian branches or an SBI foreign office, subject to currency and regulatory rules

image.alt: State Bank of India keyhole mark for NRI Loan Against Deposits

facts.label: Facility types
facts.value: Demand loan or overdraft against NRO/NRE/FCNR(B); foreign-currency loan additionally available against FCNR(B)
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits
facts.quoteOrContext: The Features table lists demand loan and overdraft under all three security columns and adds foreign-currency loan under FCNR(B).

facts.label: Published maximum loan
facts.value: No maximum limit stated in the product table
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits
facts.quoteOrContext: The Maximum Loan row displays 'No limit' under all three deposit-security columns.

facts.label: Facility type
facts.value: At a branch, SBI offers a demand loan or overdraft against NRO, NRE or FCNR(B) deposits; against FCNR(B), a foreign-currency demand loan is also listed.
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits; Global Connect NRI April 2025
facts.pageOrSection: Product page Overview and Features — Type of facility; newsletter PDF p.21
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI lists demand loan and overdraft for rupee deposit-backed facilities; FCNR(B) additionally has a foreign-currency loan. The online NRI overdraft is a separate product and is not represented here.

facts.label: Deposit security
facts.value: NRO TDR/STDR/RD; NRE TDR/STDR/RD; or FCNR(B) TDR/STDR. SBI marks a lien on the underlying deposit for a deposit-backed loan.
facts.documentTitle: Loan Against Time Deposit — SBI Personal Banking
facts.pageOrSection: Features — Security Lien; Branch eligibility includes NRE/NRO/FCNR(B) deposits
facts.quoteOrContext: The current branch-level terms list TDR/STDR/RD, expressly include NRE/NRO and FCNR(B) deposits, and identify a lien on the underlying time deposit.

facts.label: Loan use
facts.value: SBI permits personal use, direct investment in India on a non-repatriation basis, an Indian home/flat for the borrower's own residence, emergency needs and business activity. It prohibits re-lending, agricultural or plantation activity, investment in a real-estate business, and remitting the loan amount abroad.
facts.documentTitle: SBI FAQ for NRI; NRI Loan against Deposits — SBI
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ Loans questions 3–4; NRI product page Overview — purpose and repatriation
facts.quoteOrContext: The NRI FAQ enumerates personal use, non-repatriation direct investment and own residence; the NRI loan page adds emergency/business wording and repeats the prohibited-use restrictions.

facts.label: Use outside India
facts.value: The loan proceeds cannot be remitted or repatriated outside India.
facts.documentTitle: NRI Loan against Deposits — SBI; FAQ for NRI
facts.quoteOrContext: The page and FAQ both state that loan proceeds cannot be remitted abroad.

facts.label: Loan currency
facts.value: NRO/NRE facilities are in Indian rupees. FCNR(B) security supports an Indian-rupee facility or, where offered, a foreign-currency demand loan in USD, GBP or EUR.
facts.documentTitle: NRI Loan against Deposits — SBI; Global Connect NRI April 2025
facts.pageOrSection: Features — Currency and facility; newsletter PDF p.21
facts.quoteOrContext: The NRI table lists rupees for NRE/NRO and rupees plus USD, GBP and EUR for FCNR(B); foreign-currency lending is only against FCNR(B).

facts.label: Loan period
facts.value: Rupee loans run up to the remaining maturity of the pledged deposit. An FCNR(B)-backed foreign-currency loan may run for 1, 2 or 3 years or the deposit's remaining maturity, whichever is applicable; SBI specifies a one-year minimum.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Global Connect NRI newsletter — April 2025
facts.quoteOrContext: The newsletter separates rupee and foreign-currency tenure; the foreign-currency loan is available for 1, 2 or 3 years or remaining deposit maturity, with a one-year minimum also stated on the product page.

facts.label: Minimum loan amount
facts.value: NRO/NRE rupee loans: no minimum amount stated in the NRI table. FCNR(B): minimum ₹25,000 for an INR loan; for a foreign-currency loan, USD 25,000, GBP 15,000 or EUR 20,000. SBI's general branch page says branch advances have no specific minimum; the NRI-specific amounts are retained for the FCNR(B) variants.
facts.unit: minimum loan amounts by loan currency
facts.documentTitle: SBI Global Connect NRI newsletter — April 2025; Loan Against Time Deposit — SBI Personal Banking
facts.pageOrSection: Newsletter PDF p.21 — Minimum Loan; generic branch-level page FAQ question 7
facts.quoteOrContext: The NRI-specific table gives no limit for NRE/NRO and numeric FCNR(B) thresholds; the general page says no specific minimum at branches. The specific FCNR amounts are shown with their NRI variant scope, not applied to other branches.

facts.label: Maximum loan / available against deposit
facts.value: No absolute rupee ceiling is stated for the branch facility. SBI's current branch-level page and NRE/NRO pages say lending may reach 90% of deposit value (the NRE/NRO pages include accrued interest). The NRI-specific table instead publishes margin schedules that can imply different advance percentages, including 95% at a 5% margin. SBI does not explain how the 90% cap and maturity-based NRI schedules interact; confirm the applicable drawable percentage with the branch.
facts.documentTitle: Loan Against Time Deposit — SBI Personal Banking; NRI Loan against Deposits; NRE/NRO Account pages
facts.pageOrSection: General page Features and Branch eligibility; NRI table — Maximum Loan and Margin; NRE/NRO account pages — Loans Against Deposits
facts.quoteOrContext: The general page sets 90% of time-deposit value for the branch facility; NRE/NRO pages repeat 90%, while the NRI-specific dated margin table includes 5% margin in one band. These statements are recorded together without claiming one overrides the other.

facts.label: Margin against deposit — source schedules differ
facts.value: Current general branch terms: minimum 10% for up to 5 years or remaining deposit maturity, and 15% for a demand loan beyond 5 years up to 10 years or remaining maturity. The NRI-specific schedule separately lists NRE/NRO rupee margins of 5%, 10% or 15% by deposit residual maturity; FCNR(B) rupee margins of 10%, 20%, 30%, 40% or 50%; and FCNR(B) foreign-currency margins of 10% or 15%. SBI has not clarified which schedule controls each NRI branch facility.
facts.documentTitle: Loan Against Time Deposit — SBI Personal Banking; NRI Loan against Deposits; Global Connect NRI April 2025
facts.pageOrSection: General page Features — Margin; NRI product page Features — Margin; newsletter PDF pp.21–22
facts.quoteOrContext: Both official sources cover branch deposit-backed lending; the newer shared page includes NRE/NRO/FCNR(B), while the NRI-specific document gives different collateral-margin bands. SBI publishes no crosswalk or exception explaining the difference.

facts.label: Interest rate
facts.value: NRO/NRE rupee loan: 1.00 percentage point above the pledged time-deposit rate. FCNR(B)-backed rupee loan: 2.90 percentage points above one-year MCLR. FCNR(B)-backed foreign-currency loan: 150 basis points above the applicable FCNR(B) deposit rate.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Loans Against Securities and Consumer Durable Loans — rate table; NRI Loan against Deposits — SBI
facts.pageOrSection: Loan Against Bank Time Deposit/FCNR(B) rates effective 15 August 2025; NRI page Interest rate on Rupee Loan and Foreign Currency Loan
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI's detailed 2025 loan-rate section names the NRE/NRO and FCNR(B) formulas. The NRI product table also publishes the 150-basis-point foreign-currency spread.

facts.label: FCNR(B)-backed rupee-loan rate
facts.value: 2.90 percentage points over one-year MCLR. SBI's one-year MCLR is 8.70% effective 15 September 2026, giving a derived current indicative rate of 11.60% p.a.; this is not an APR and can change when MCLR changes.
facts.documentTitle: SBI MCLR effective 15 September 2026; SBI Loan Against Securities and Consumer Durable Loans rate table
facts.pageOrSection: MCLR tenor table — One Year 8.70%; loan-rate table — FCNR(B) 2.90% over one-year MCLR
facts.quoteOrContext: 11.60% is arithmetic from SBI's current benchmark and published spread (8.70 + 2.90), not a separately published APR or flat all-currency rate.

facts.label: Benchmark
facts.value: One-year MCLR for the FCNR(B)-backed rupee loan; 8.70% effective 15 September 2026. NRO/NRE and foreign-currency loans instead use the pledged deposit's applicable contracted rate plus SBI's published spread.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate
facts.pageOrSection: Tenor-wise MCLR table effective 15 September 2026 — One Year
facts.quoteOrContext: The current one-year MCLR is 8.70%; SBI's FCNR(B) rupee-loan formula is 2.90 percentage points above that benchmark.

facts.label: FCNR(B) foreign-currency loan rate
facts.value: 150 basis points (1.50 percentage points) above the interest rate applicable to the pledged FCNR(B) deposit; the actual rate therefore depends on that deposit's currency, tenor and contracted rate.
facts.documentTitle: SBI Global Connect NRI newsletter — April 2025; NRI Loan against Deposits — SBI
facts.pageOrSection: Newsletter PDF p.22 — Interest rate on Foreign Currency; NRI product page Features — same row
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI specifies 150 BPS over the applicable FCNR(B) deposit rate, not a single universal foreign-currency loan rate.

facts.label: Interest charging
facts.value: Interest on both rupee and foreign-currency loans is charged at monthly intervals.
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits; Global Connect NRI April 2025
facts.pageOrSection: Overview — Interest; newsletter PDF p.22 — Interest charged
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI says interest is charged at monthly intervals for INR and foreign-currency loans.

facts.label: Processing fee
facts.value: ₹0 — SBI states zero processing charges for the branch-level Loan Against Time Deposit facility, which expressly includes NRE/NRO and FCNR(B) deposits.
facts.documentTitle: Loan Against Time Deposit — SBI Personal Banking
facts.pageOrSection: Features — Zero processing charges; Eligibility — branch route includes NRE/NRO/FCNR(B)
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI lists zero processing charges, then explicitly says branch loans are available against NRE/NRO/FCNR(B) deposits. The 2018 NRI tariff is kept as historical context and does not override this current product page.

facts.label: Prepayment charge
facts.value: ₹0 — SBI states that there are no prepayment penalties for its branch-level Loan Against Time Deposit facility, including loans against NRE/NRO/FCNR(B) deposits.
facts.documentTitle: Loan Against Time Deposit — SBI Personal Banking
facts.pageOrSection: Features — No prepayment penalties; Branch eligibility includes NRE/NRO/FCNR(B)
facts.quoteOrContext: The current source states no prepayment penalties for this deposit-loan facility and explicitly includes branch NRI deposits.

facts.label: Underlying-deposit premature withdrawal
facts.value: NRE and FCNR(B): premature withdrawal is not permitted while used as security. NRO: withdrawal is permitted after outstanding principal and interest are settled first.
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits
facts.pageOrSection: Overview — Premature withdrawal of underlying deposit
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI's NRI product page says premature withdrawal is not permissible for NRE/FCNR(B); NRO can be withdrawn only after principal and interest are settled.

facts.label: Repayment
facts.value: NRO: adjust the underlying deposit, pay by fresh inward remittance or use another NRO account. NRE: adjust the underlying deposit at maturity, pay by fresh inward remittance or use an NRO/NRE account; NRO-account repayment is within the USD 1 million per-financial-year cap. FCNR(B): adjust the FCNR(B) deposit at maturity, pay by fresh inward remittance or use an NRO/NRE account, with the same NRO repayment cap.
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits; Global Connect NRI April 2025
facts.pageOrSection: Features — Repayment of Loan; newsletter PDF p.22 — Repayment
facts.quoteOrContext: The page and newsletter separate NRO, NRE and FCNR(B) repayment routes; for NRE/FCNR(B), adjustment of the underlying deposit is at maturity only. NRO-account repayment is capped at USD 1 million per financial year.

facts.label: Application and document execution
facts.value: For a branch loan, contact the deposit's SBI home branch and submit the loan request. In India, the depositor must execute the loan documents in person at the home branch; a Power of Attorney holder cannot execute them. SBI's NRI forms index does not list a deposit-loan-specific application or fixed attachment checklist.
facts.documentTitle: SBI FAQ for NRI; Download Forms — NRI
facts.pageOrSection: FAQ Loans question 5; NRI Loan Features — Execution of Documents; Download Forms — complete new account/deposit/loan index
facts.quoteOrContext: SBI directs branch applicants to the home branch for a loan request and specifies depositor execution. The forms index lists NRI home/car loans and account forms but no loan-against-deposit form or specific checklist.

facts.label: APR

normalizedValue.reason: SBI publishes deposit-linked spreads and an MCLR-linked formula for this branch facility, but no separate APR calculation in the full NRI page, current time-deposit loan page or applicable rate table.

facts.pageOrSection: Full eligibility/security sections, FAQ Loans, and NRI Download Forms index
facts.quoteOrContext: These sources define an eligible depositor and pledged deposit but do not publish an income threshold. Public comparison value intentionally remains blank.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: India-branch loan: the borrower must own the pledged NRO, NRE or FCNR(B) deposit. Internet Banking overdraft: single-name NRE/NRO fixed deposits with at least 6 months remaining; joint deposits are ineligible. Selected SBI foreign offices separately allow third-party loans against NRE/FCNR(B), but not NRO.
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits; SBI FAQ for NRI
facts.pageOrSection: Product Overview and Features — borrower and channel rows; FAQ Loans questions 2, 5–7
facts.quoteOrContext: The product page says loans against NRE/NRO/FCNR(B) deposits are given to the depositor only and lists Internet Banking OD as available for NRE/NRO deposits. The FAQ states online OD is limited to single-holder NRE/NRO fixed deposits with at least six months remaining, excludes joint holders, requires mapping of certain offline-opened deposits, bars third-party borrowing in India, and describes a selected-foreign-office exception for NRE/FCNR(B), not NRO.

facts.label: Borrower and application route
facts.value: For a branch loan, apply through the deposit's home branch; for an India-branch facility, the depositor must execute documents personally, not through a Power of Attorney holder. Internet Banking OD is separate: single-name NRE/NRO fixed deposits (TDR/STDR/eTDR/eSTDR) with at least 6 months remaining are eligible; joint deposits are not, and fixed deposits opened outside Internet Banking must be mapped. The FAQ separately says selected SBI foreign offices may lend to third parties against NRE/FCNR(B), but not NRO.
facts.documentTitle: SBI NRI Loan against Deposits; SBI FAQ for NRI
facts.pageOrSection: Product Features — channel availability and execution; FAQ Loans questions 2, 5–7
facts.quoteOrContext: The current page lists Internet Banking overdraft as available for NRE and NRO deposits. The current FAQ gives the specific online holder and six-month term conditions and distinguishes third-party lending in India from the selected foreign-office facility. This corrects the prior canonical wording that wrongly stated NRE TDR/STDR were excluded from online creation.

requiredDocuments: Loan documents executed personally by the depositor at the home branch in India; a power-of-attorney holder cannot execute them
For a facility through an overseas branch, documents required under that SBI foreign office's policy

benefits: Choose an unsecured daily-reducing-balance term loan or an overdraft with reducing drawing power; no security or guarantor is required.
Published borrowing ranges from ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh, subject to SBI's income and EMI/NMI limits.
Repayment can run from 6 to 84 months, subject to retirement, contract end or the applicable age limit.
SBI lists a provision for a second loan and digital document execution.
Optional SBI Life group cover and SBI General loan insurance are offered through the application form; neither is mandatory for the loan application.
eligibilityNotes: Eligible employment groups listed on the current page are Central/State Government, Railway, Police, PSU, Defence, Indian Coast Guard, Central Armed Police and corporate employees.
An SBI Salary Package Account is required. Minimum service is 6 months for Government/Defence employees and 12 months for Corporate employees.
Minimum net monthly salary is ₹20,000 for Government/Defence employees and ₹25,000 for Corporate employees. The applicant must be an Indian national and meet SBI's credit policy.
Published age is 21–60 years. Serving Government/Defence employees above 60 may be considered case by case; approval is not assured.
The maximum amount is the lower of the amount supported by an EMI/NMI ratio up to 65% and 30 times net monthly income; the maximum is not an entitlement.
requiredDocuments: Current product page: PAN; six months' salary slips; employer identity card, service certificate, contract letter or canteen ID; latest ITR/Form 16 if applicable; and six months of statements for the account receiving salary credits.

Current product page KYC route: fully KYC-compliant existing SBI customers with unchanged details need no fresh KYC set; customers with changed details submit only relevant update documents; PAN is mandatory if it is not seeded in SBI's CBS.

English Xpress Credit application form: two latest passport-size photographs; identity and residence proofs; employer identity card; six months' salary-credit account statement; and latest-month salary slip or Form 16 (marked optional except for specified employee groups).

For the salary check-off route, the Xpress Credit form also lists irrevocable authority letters addressed to the disbursing authority and from the person authorized to disburse salary and allowances. The relevant route and applicable KYC/document list should be confirmed with SBI because the form and product-page checklists differ in detail.

products.name: Union Rooftop Solar Loan (URTS)
customerSegments: Individuals with an existing independent house
products.summary: Retail finance for a grid-connected rooftop solar system up to 25 kW on an existing independent house, with a published 75%/₹10 lakh quantum cap, subsidy and security rules.
benefits: Grid-connected rooftop solar up to 25 kW
Maximum 75% of approved project cost or ₹10 lakh, whichever is lower
5% borrower margin
Up to 20-year repayment period
eligibilityNotes: Existing independent house; applicant must not have another-bank/FI loan against the same house under the FAQ terms.
requiredDocuments: Application, KYC, project cost/approval documents, house/property documents and documents requested by Union Bank.

facts.label: Maximum amount
facts.value: Maximum finance is 75% of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy-approved project cost or ₹10 lakh, whichever is lower.
facts.documentTitle: Union Roof Top Solar (URTS) frequent-answer PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ states maximum quantum is 75% of MNRE-approved project cost or Rs.10 lakh, whichever is lower.

facts.label: Interest rate
facts.value: URTS interest starts from 6.80% p.a., linked to EBLR, under the reviewed official FAQ.
facts.documentTitle: Union Roof Top Solar (URTS) frequent-answer PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ states URTS interest starts from 6.80% p.a. linked to EBLR.

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: For an individual with an existing independent house installing a grid-connected rooftop solar system up to 25 kW; the FAQ says the borrower should not have another bank/FI loan against the same house.
facts.documentTitle: Union Rooftop Solar / URTS FAQ
facts.quoteOrContext: The product page limits the scheme to residential grid-connected rooftop systems up to 25 kW; the FAQ states the existing-house and no-other-loan condition.

facts.label: Margin
facts.value: Borrower margin is 5% of the project cost.
facts.documentTitle: Union Roof Top Solar (URTS) frequent-answer PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ states margin to be brought by the URTS borrower is 5%.

facts.label: Subsidy
facts.value: MNRE subsidy: 40% of project cost for installation up to 3 kW, and 20% for above 3 kW up to 10 kW; subsidy is provided through the State DISCOM and used toward project finance along with borrower margin.
facts.documentTitle: Union Roof Top Solar (URTS) frequent-answer PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ publishes 40% and 20% subsidy bands and the MNRE/State DISCOM flow.

facts.label: Tenure
facts.value: Repayment is up to 20 years in EMI or the Union Home Loan repayment period, whichever is earlier.
facts.documentTitle: Union Roof Top Solar (URTS) frequent-answer PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ states repayment period is 20 years in EMI or the Union Home Loan period, whichever is earlier.

facts.label: Moratorium
facts.value: Maximum 6 months or the time taken by the DISCOM for installation, whichever is earlier.
facts.documentTitle: Union Roof Top Solar (URTS) frequent-answer PDF
facts.quoteOrContext: The FAQ states maximum moratorium is six months or installation time, whichever is earlier.

facts.label: Security
facts.value: Primary security is hypothecation of the rooftop solar panel. Collateral is nil up to ₹1 lakh; above ₹1 lakh, an existing-home borrower continues the house mortgage, while a new customer provides assignment of LIC policy or lien on FD for 100% of loan amount.

facts.label: Co-borrower liability
facts.value: The July 2026 agreement says co-borrowers are jointly and severally liable for the agreement obligations.

facts.label: Use of funds
facts.value: The agreement restricts use of the loan to the purpose stated in the application and excludes speculative, illegal or anti-social purposes.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 3 says the loan may be used only for the purpose stated in the application, not for capital-market investment or speculative, illegal or anti-social purposes.

facts.label: Cancellation timing and settlement
facts.value: YES BANK may suspend or cancel a facility not used within 15 days of its disbursement instruction. The borrower may cancel within 15 days of disbursement; the agreement also describes a review-based option within 15 days after signing the terms. In either clause, cancellation takes effect only after the full outstanding balance, interest and charges are paid or returned within the specified period.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 3 gives the borrower a 15-day cancellation window from disbursement and requires full payment of the outstanding balance; clause 6 separately measures a review option from signing these terms and states that continued use/retention of funds implies acceptance.

facts.label: Education discontinuation and refunds
facts.value: If admission is cancelled, a visa is rejected, the student changes college or the education pursuit otherwise ends, the borrower must seek any refund from the institution and use a refund received to repay the outstanding loan.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 12 lists admission cancellation, visa rejection, college change and other end of study as examples; refund amounts must be used to repay the balance.

facts.label: Return of original security documents
facts.value: Original security/property documents submitted for the facility are to be returned within 30 days after full repayment and closure. YES BANK also says it will issue a no-objection certificate for removal of the registered charge; documents may be collected at a Retail Asset Loan Centre.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: The agreement sets a 30-day return period after full payment and account closure, requires the Bank to issue an NOC for charge removal, and names a Retail Asset Loan Centre as a collection location.

facts.label: Loan disbursement
facts.value: YES BANK may disburse the sanctioned loan in full or in part at its discretion; the sanctioned schedule sets the facility ceiling.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: The agreement says the loan cannot exceed the amount in its schedule and YES BANK may disburse all or part of it at its discretion.

facts.label: Charges for inaccurate requested information
facts.value: If information or documents requested by the Bank contain a discrepancy, error or misrepresentation, YES BANK may, at its discretion, levy penal charges under the applicable Schedule of Charges or additional interest. The agreement does not state the amount here.
facts.unit: contract condition; amount not specified in this agreement clause
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: The clause concerns statements, records or documents requested based on the loan and permits a penal charge under the SOC or additional interest if the submission contains an error, discrepancy or misrepresentation.

facts.label: Final rate and repayment terms
facts.value: The welcome letter and repayment schedule form part of the loan agreement. YES BANK says the exact principal-interest split and other charges will be provided in the welcome letter and will bind the borrower.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 7 incorporates the welcome letter and repayment schedule and places the exact principal/interest breakup and other charges in the welcome letter.

facts.label: Missed-payment classification
facts.value: The agreement says missed, delayed or failed repayments may result in Special Mention Account (SMA) or Non-Performing Asset (NPA) classification under the Reserve Bank of India's applicable guidelines. Day-based criteria and a date-based illustration are present in the agreement; their table text is retained separately pending visual layout verification.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 7 subjects facility classification to RBI guidelines and states a default or delay can result in SMA and/or NPA classification.

facts.label: Future government fees and levies
facts.value: The borrower agrees to pay charges, fees, service charges or levies imposed in future by government authorities or government-created entities, including those resulting from new or amended rules and laws.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 9 makes future government and government-entity charges and levies payable by the borrower, including those arising from new rules or amendments.

facts.label: Recovery and information sharing
facts.value: The Bank may appoint third parties to administer or collect the loan, contact the borrower and perform related lawful tasks; the agreement authorizes disclosure to them of relevant borrower and loan information.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 10 authorizes appointment of third parties for loan administration and recovery and disclosure of necessary or relevant borrower and loan information to them.

facts.label: Education loan complaint route
facts.value: Complaints can be sent to yestouch@yes.bank.in or 1800 1200. If unresolved within the communicated timeframe, the agreement lists head.grievanceredressal@yesbank.in and +91 22 5079 5173 for escalation. It says YES BANK will resolve complaints within 30 days; unresolved complaints may be escalated to the Banking Ombudsman or RBI's Customer Education and Protection Cell.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 11 provides the stated first-level and grievance-officer contacts, a 30-day resolution commitment, and the RBI escalation options.

facts.label: Dispute resolution
facts.value: The agreement provides for arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, administered by Presolv with a sole arbitrator; if Presolv cannot administer, it names CNICA as the fallback. The seat and venue are the disbursing branch location, proceedings are in English, and virtual hearings or online dispute resolution are permitted.
facts.documentTitle: Education Loan Agreement — body Version July 2026
facts.quoteOrContext: Clause 5 identifies Presolv, the CNICA fallback, arbitration rules, venue, language and virtual/ODR options.
